picks.headline: No. 13 Texas Tech vs. No. 22 Arizona Football Game Preview and Prediction
picks.blurb: No. 13 Texas Tech vs. No. 22 Arizona Football Game Preview and Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Texas Tech Athletics Texas Tech hosts Arizona in this big time Big 12 showdown. The Texas Tech Red Raiders need to focus on boosting their offense for this one. Quarterback Will Hammond has 1,561 passing yards, but he has thrown only six touchdowns and has six interceptions on the season. Explosive running back J'Koby Williams has 619 rushing yards and 5 TDs, but if you take away the Arizona State and Oregon State games, he has been inconsistent for the Red Raiders this season. Kenny Johnson , a receiver, is the main downfield target but only has one touchdown reception this season and, besides the Houston and Arizona State games, has not had a significant impact on the Texas Tech passing attack. All three as well as some other key offensive players need to step up and have big games against Arizona to win this game. The defense has to get back to focusing and dominating like they have for a lot of the season. The Red Raiders have one of the most ball-hawking secondary units in the country, sitting near the top of NCAA FBS with 13 interceptions. Defensive lineman A.J. Holmes Jr. anchors the front seven and has 6 sacks this season. However, the Red Raiders are coming off their first loss of the season, a 37-24 loss to Cincinnati where they gave up 427 yards and gave up four passing touchdowns. They will be seeking to bounce back at home to stay undefeated at home this season. Arizona, on the other hand, has a five-game winning streak and defeated Cincinnati by a final score of 34-7. Their only loss of the season was to BYU on the road. Veteran quarterback Noah Fifita leads the Arizona Wildcats, who again have a high-efficiency passing offense, with Fifiti already having 2,064 passing yards and 18 TDs through seven games. Kedrick Reescano leads the ground game with just over 300 rushing yards and five touchdowns, while wideout Isaiah Mizell is an explosive playmaker with 493 yards and 5 TDs this season, most of which have come in the Wildcats' last two games against Iowa State and West Virginia. Linebacker Taye Brown has a team-leading 27 tackles and leads the Wildcats defense. Edge rusher Chase Kennedy leads the team in pressure rate with 4 sacks, and the Texas Tech offensive line has a tough task trying to stop him from getting to the quarterback. Arizona has a scoring defense that gives up only 16.7 points per game, but they did give up 31 points against West Virginia. Arizona recently crushed Iowa State 39-3 and has put up a total of just over 200 points in their last five games. The Wildcats are also 2-1 on the road this season heading into Lubbock for this top 25 game. The key matchup for this game will be Noah Fifita vs. the Texas Tech secondary. Fifita’s efficient throwing (almost 74% completion rate) will face immediate tests from a Red Raider defense that excels at creating takeaways via interceptions. Another major matchup in this game pits the Red Raiders offensive line against Arizona’s front seven on defense. Texas Tech’s running offense behind J’Koby Williams and Quinten Joyner will face a challenge against an Arizona front seven that is holding opponents under 110 rushing yards per game. This game also has Big 12 Championship ramifications since both teams are deadlocked at 3-1 in conference play behind undefeated Utah, and the winner is squarely in the race for a Big 12 Championship Game berth. An early game prediction for this game that may change slightly as the injury reports for both teams come out later this week, but the Red Raiders bounce back and win a very close game by a final score of Texas Tech 28, Arizona 27. Arizona has been fantastic ever since its 28-17 loss at BYU early in the season, including a 34-7 win over Cincinnati. But it still has a few nasty games to go in November. Both teams are 6-1. The winner will be set up nicely for a College Football Playoff spot if it doesn't win the Big 12 title. The loser will still be alive for the CFP if it wins out, but getting to the Big 12 Championship in a loaded conference season will be tough. Arizona vs Texas Tech: Quick Hits Texas Tech still has to go to Oklahoma State, but it doesn't have to face BYU or Utah, and the other three games against West Virginia, at Baylor, and TCU aren't bad. Arizona gets three of its final four games at home, getting TCU and Utah next before going to Kansas State and finishing up against Arizona State. Texas Tech won the most recent matchup 28-22 in 2024 and is 5-2-1 in the series going back to 1975. How To Watch Arizona vs Texas Tech Arizona at Texas Tech Date: Saturday, October 31, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: ESPN Location: Galaxy Stadium, Lubbock, TX – Week 9 Schedule, Game Previews – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predicting the First CFP Top 25 – CFN Week 9 Expert Picks Why Arizona Will Win For the second time all year, Texas Tech played someone who could run well, and Cincinnati went off in the 13-point win. Houston can run. It ran 37 times for 175 yards against the Red Raiders, and lost when it couldn't hit a late two-point conversion. Cincinnati wasn't exactly more physical, but it found space on the way to a 255-yard day with big run after big run. Arizona's running game isn't a killer, but it's more than effective enough, working hand-in-hand with super-accurate quarterback Noah Fifita and an offense that's great at keeping the chains moving. Why Texas Tech Will Win Arizona doesn't take the ball away enough, and that matters in a huge way here. The Wildcats forced two takeaways in the win over Washington State, and two more in the win over West Virginia. That's about it, coming up with six on the year. Texas Tech has a huge problem with turnovers, with three against Cincinnati, two against Houston, and ten in the last five games. Don't turn it over, or at least stay even in the mistake battle, and the Red Raiders should be fine. Texas Tech has a great balance to its attack, and it needs to mix it up. BYU and West Virginia – in very different ways – both showed it's possible to move the ball efficiently against the Wildcat defense. Arizona vs Texas Tech Prediction, Betting Lines Is Arizona ready to show that it's really and truly a player, or will Texas Tech wipe away the Cincinnati loss like it was just a blip? It'll be a little of both, as Arizona controls the clock and tempo for the first half, but Texas Tech gets the pass rush working early in the second half. It'll be rough for the Red Raiders without pressuring Fifita, and they won't do enough of it over the final ten minutes. Texas Tech expert previews the Arizona football game, makes a score prediction
picks.blurb: Texas Tech expert previews the Arizona Wildcats football game, makes a score prediction | Arizona Desert Swarm Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo An Arizona Wildcats Community Arizona Desert Swarm October 29, 2026 Arizona Desert Swarm Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Arizona Basketball Arizona Football Arizona Softball Arizona Recruiting Arizona Soccer Arizona Volleyball Arizona Baseball Arizona Gymnastics Arizona in the Pros Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Arizona Football Odds Arizona Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Arizona Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Arizona Football College football has one of the longest offseasons of any sport, which lends itself to certain players and teams generating a lot of hype and attention. Texas Tech falls squarely in that category, as its seemingly unlimited resources thanks to billionaire booster Cody Campbell made it a go-to place for top transfers out of the portal. But that also led to the ill-fated acquisition of quarterback Brendan Sorsby , who after leaving Cincinnati for Tech was revealed to have bet on college sports. Sorsby was banned by the NCAA, later reinstated, but the backlash led to him leaving the program before ever playing a game. Despite that, Tech was unbeaten before losing last week, dropping to No. 13 in the AP poll and into a tie for second place in the Big 12 with, among other teams, Arizona. That in effect makes Saturday’s matchup an unofficial elimination game for the conference title race. To better understand the Red Raiders, we reached out to Seth Jungman of Staking the Plains for some insight and a score prediction. Below are his eloquent answers to our inarticulate questions: AZ Desert Swarm: Outside of the irony of the first loss coming to Cincinnati, what were the biggest contributors to Texas Tech falling from the ranks of the unbeatens? Seth Jungman: “It’s the thing that I think Texas Tech fans have known, but maybe the national media wasn’t paying attention. I think most fans have known that the offense simply wasn’t very good and the defense isn’t as good as it was last year. Will Hammond is fine, but there’s a reason why the staff went out to get Brendan Sorsby before the season. They knew he probably wasn’t ready, but things happened and here we are. Also, I think it’s incredibly evident that the players who were part of this defense last year were truly special, particularly Jacob Rodriguez, David Bailey, and Romello Height. Getting to the quarterback to wreck offenses was the cheat code last year and this year, that’s simply not happening.” It’s fair to say that Will Hammond was not the first choice to lead this offense. How do you think he has performed to this point? What are his best attributes and where does he lack most? “I thought last week against Arizona State he took a step forward, but against Cincinnati he took two steps back. His best attributes is that he is a natural leader and he wants the ball in his hands and he wants to be the guy. My biggest problem with him is that I think he makes bad game management decisions. Knowing that the team needs points, he’ll heave the ball towards the end zone with a low chance of completion rather than take the play that keeps the drive alive. His lack of understanding of knowing when to take chances and when to churn yards is what bothers me the most.” What is the likelihood that Cameron Dickey will be back for this game? How would that impact the run game and the way J’Koby Williams, who has run for 680 yards and five touchdowns, get used? “I think chances are very good that he returns. It’s been about four weeks from the dreaded high-ankle sprain and that’s about the time. I don’t think it was a bad sprain so this game would seem about right and he was out doing some drills this past week. What Dickey offers is a guy that’s going to bruise and batter the opposing defense while Williams will break a 40-yard run in what looks like a lost play. Quinten Joyner has tried to fill that roll for Dickey, but it’s not the same. Joyner is coming off of ACL surgery and he doesn’t have the same burst he had at USC. I think the staff will likely get back to that Dickey-Williams rotation as soon as possible.” Texas Tech is second in FBS in passes intercepted (13) but has also given up 16 TD passes and is ranked third-worst in the Big 12 in pass defense. How do you expect the defense to try and stop Noah Fifita? “As mentioned above, the Texas Tech defense last year was getting to the quarterback so quickly that teams simply could not function offensively. This year . . . not so much. Fifita has rounded out to be such a good quarterback, I truly expect him to have a very good day. There’s almost no difference between his home and road stats, three picks on the road and just one at home, and he’s throwing for nearly 300 yards every time he steps on the field. That’s the kind of consistency that you expect from a senior and with Fifita’s ability to run to keep the defense honest, I expect him to do what he’s done all year long.” Who are the top defensive players that Arizona has to be most concerned with? “Defensive tackle AJ Holmes is an absolute unit and there aren’t a ton of defensive tackles that truly rush the passer, but he’s one of them. The linebacking corps is incredibly solid with Ben Roberts, John Curry and Austin Romaine. I’ll also add in Brice Pollock at cornerback. The pass defense is struggling a bit, but he’s a solid cornerback that can make plays.” Considering all the money that was spent on this team, and all the national attention it has brought on itself—thanks, Cody Campbell!—does it feel like the season is on the line in this game? How do you expect Tech to respond to that last performance? “As you have already recognized, this team is a quarterback short of maybe what it could have been. I try not to involve myself in the offseason drama. The whole thing was a mess and handled poorly. I think we’ve all moved on, but I know it still lingers and I think that Sorsby would have made a significant difference in the offense. For what Joey McGuire preaches, yes, the season is on the brink because the goal is to win the Big 12 and make the playoffs. I don’t know that a Big 12 team with two losses makes the playoff and I also don’t think that a 2-loss Big 12 team makes the championship. “I do expect Texas Tech to play much better than what they did against Cincinnati and I think it will be a much more competitive game. I also realize that Arizona’s defense is no joke and the Texas Tech offense has really only played well against defenses that aren’t very good. The offense and defense for the Red Raiders have a lot to prove against Arizona.” Prediction time. Does Arizona end the Red Raiders’ 12-game home win streak and continue its push toward the Big 12 title game or does Texas Tech get back on track? Give us a score pick. “My gut tells me that this will be an incredibly close game and Vegas thinks so as well. With a touchdown advantage, the line now sits at Texas Tech -3.5. I tend to agree, that despite the flaws that were on display against Cincinnati, I think Texas Tech does win the game, but I’d take Arizona and those points. picks.blurb: Arizona vs. Texas Tech Prediction, Pick and Odds for Week 9 Teams Arizona Wildcats Arizona State Sun Devils Cincinnati Bearcats Colorado Buffaloes Houston Cougars Iowa State Cyclones Kansas Jayhawks Kansas State Wildcats Oklahoma State Cowboys TCU Horned Frogs Texas Tech Red Raiders West Virginia Mountaineers Former Foes Missouri Tigers Nebraska Cornhuskers Oklahoma Sooners Texas A&M Aggies Texas Longhorns Recruiting Football Transfer Portal Video Watch on YouTube Listen on Apple Listen on Spotify Forum Members Login Heartland College Sports – An Independent Big 12 Today Blog | College Football News | Big 12 Today The Arizona Wildcats and Texas Tech Red Raiders meet on Saturday in Lubbock in a Top 25 showdown that could have major implications on the Big 12 Championship race. Both teams enter Week 9 at 6-1 overall and 3-1 in Big 12 play, but they're coming off completely different Saturdays. Arizona made another statement by crushing Iowa State 39-3, while Texas Tech suffered its first loss of the season in a 37-24 road defeat at Cincinnati. Now, Texas Tech returns home to a place where it has won 12 straight games, while Arizona gets another opportunity to prove it belongs among the top contenders in the Big 12. The matchup also features an intriguing battle between Noah Fifita and an aggressive Texas Tech defense that leads the country with five pick-sixes this season. Here is everything you need to know about Arizona vs. Texas Tech in Week 9, including our prediction and pick for Saturday's Big 12 showdown. Texas Tech vs. Arizona Odds Spread: Texas Tech -3.5 Over/Under: 54.5 Moneyline: Arizona +134/Texas Tech -160 Odds as of Tuesday afternoon. Odds are subject to change. The Biggest Question: Arizona's Passing Game vs. Texas Tech's Defense? The Red Raiders' defense has been underwhelming, at best. Texas Tech ranks 14th in the Big 12 Conference in passing yards allowed per game, ranking only ahead of Cincinnati and West Virginia. Now, this secondary does have 13 takeaways, which is tops in the Big 12. But that also tells me that they may be too aggressive , at times. And now they have to slow down Noah Fifita, who doesn't make many mistakes. He's thrown 18 touchdowns to just four interceptions this season and has the deepest wide receiver corps in the entire Big 12. Whoever wins this match up will win the game. Houston vs. Utah Prediction and Pick Prediction: Arizona 31, Texas Tech 24 Texas Tech was exposed last week at Cincinnati. Yes, they have talent, but they haven't been able to put it all together this season. And after Saturday, there's no evidence that it's magically going to happen against one of the most underrated teams in the country, Arizona, who is playing some of the best football in America right now. Since losing to BYU on the road (a game they led in the second half), Arizona has won five-straight games by an average of nearly 24 points. I haven't even talked about the other side of the ball, where Arizona is Top 5 in passing defense in yards allowed per game, and ranked 3rd in the Big 12 in yards allowed per carry (3.1). The front seven has been outstanding, as that impressive run defense has done it against the Top 2 rushing offenses in the league (West Virginia, Cincinnati). They've racked up 24 sacks in seven games, good for second in the Big 12, and now take on a Texas Tech offensive line that has been spotty, at best, throughout the season. Also, in a game that could come down to the final drive or two, Arizona's red zone defense ranks tops in the Big 12, while Texas Tech comes in at No. 14. And as the game wears on, the Tech defense could get worn down. Tech is second-to-last in the Big 12 in Time of Possession, while Arizona is in the Top 5, this despite having a pass-heavy offense. The icing on the cake on my pick? Special teams. Arizona is the best punt returning team in the Big 12. Texas Tech ranks 13th. These little things in a tough Top 25 match up can be the difference. And they will be come Saturday in Lubbock. And if you want to know where the sharp money is: 62% of the tickets are on Texas Tech, but over 80% of the money is on Arizona. The line opened up at Arizona +4.5 and is down to +3.5. If you can still get more than a field goal, jump on it. Arizona wins. Arizona covers. away.headline: Arizona football: CB Jay’Vion Cole to miss Texas Tech game, 2 injured receivers could return
away.blurb: CB Jay’Vion Cole is listed as out on the first availability report issued by the Big 12 Conference, one of four players ruled out for the matchup with the 13th-ranked Red Raiders.. Also out are tight end Shane King and defensive linemen Kevin Moore and Ezra Funa , the latter having not played yet this season. On the offensive side, receivers Chris Hunter and Giovanni Richardson are listed as questionable. Both have missed the past two games after getting hurt Oct. 3 vs. Cincinnati, the same game fellow WR Tre Spivey suffered a season-ending injury. Tight end Cole Rusk , who has been out several games, is listed as doubtful. Also listed as questionable are running back Ismail Mahdi and linebacker Max Harris but not because of injury. Both are seeking another emergency injunction to restore their eligibility after each appeared in a few games earlier this season. For Texas Tech, running back Cameron Dickey is listed as questionable. He’s missed the last two games with an ankle injury. Arizona could get back a pair of injured wide receivers for Saturday’s Top 25 showdown at Texas Tech, but it will also be without its lockdown corner Cole had started the first seven games this season, allowing only 16 catches on 30 targets, and is among the top-graded corners in the Big 12. In his absence the UA is likely to start Dwight Bootle II, who has been part of a 3-man rotation at the two corner spots with Cole and Tyrese Boss. Slot DB Malcolm Hartzog Jr. could also see time at corner.

None of the backups have any real experience. It will be even tougher considering they are playing on the road against a conference rival. The hope is Johnson is ready to go to help the Wildcats' chance of moving three games ahead of .500.

Wisconsin is 5-2, with a very favorable November after dealing with the Hawkeyes. The winner will be deep in the College Football Playoff hunt, the loser will be out – not officially, but practically – and will be bucking for a decent bowl game. But first, someone will have to score. Just when you thought this was the new, wacky Iowa that liked to do that whole scoring points thing that the kids are all into, it's had issues in Big Ten play, losing two of the last three, including a Floyd of Rosedale-losing 13-10 game at Minnesota. Wisconsin quit pretending its offense could do much, and who needs to, with a defense that has grown into a dominant force over the last several games. Wisconsin vs Iowa: Quick Hits Wisconsin is starting a run of three road games in the next four, hosting Rutgers next week before going to Maryland and Purdue. Iowa goes on the road in two of the last three weeks, with trips to Northwestern and Illinois wrapped around Purdue. It's the 100th meeting between the two programs. Wisconsin is up 49-48-2, but Iowa has won the last four, including the last two in 2024 and 2025 by a combined score of 79-10. The Wisconsin defense was all over the USC ground game a week after holding UCLA to a Bruin season-low 120 yards in a 17-7 Badger loss. The defense had one really rough second half against Notre Dame in the season opener, and that's it. The Badgers held Penn State's offense to 13 points – the Nittany Lions got a pick six – meaning they've allowed 13 points or fewer in five of the last six games, to go along with the 17 against UCLA. Why Iowa Will Win Wisconsin has become, well … Iowa. Defense, field position, the return game, sound offense – sound familiar? And no one comes into Kinnick and out-Iowas, Iowa. Yes, the Badgers stuffed the USC running game, but Jayden Maiava and the Trojans were able to throw a little bit, hitting 62% of their passes to dink and dunk down the field. Michigan State and Penn State weren't able to throw on Wisconsin, but USC and everyone else hit at least 60% of their passes. Iowa is 4-0 when connecting on 60% or more of its throws, and 1-3 when it doesn't. Wisconsin vs Iowa Prediction, Betting Lines Iowa has been held to under 100 rushing yards four times. The losses to Ohio State and Minnesota, the 16-13 win over Iowa State, and the minor-miracle 20-19 win at Michigan. The Iowa running game has been feast-or-famine – totally dominating in the wins over everyone but Michigan. It's not going to dominate against this Badger defense, but … Wisconsin isn't completing passes. This will be about field position, mistakes, and one big play in a tough dogfight. Like the loss at UCLA, the Badgers will play well, and it won't be enough on the road. away.headline: USC Trojans Final Injury Report vs. Wisconsin Badgers
away.blurb: Left tackle Elijah Paige, a Midseason first team All-American by The Athletic, was a late add to injury report against Penn State on Oct. 10 and was ultimately held out. USC turned to true freshman Vlad Dyakonov, who made his first career start, and he excelled. But having Paige back in the lineup is a massive boost for the offensive line. The Trojans will also get back left guard Hayden Treter, who has been out since going down in the first half against Oregon on Sept. 26. Kaylon Miller has started in his place. Tight end Mark Bowman has missed each of the last two games and is questionable heading into Saturday's game against the Badgers. Having Bowman back in the lineup would impact the run and pass game. Receivers Corey Simms and Terrell Anderson are out for the season, but USC did get back freshman receiver Trent Mosley returned to the lineup against Penn State, after missing the previous three games. He was a true game time decision but immediately looked like the player that caught the attention of the college football world. Defensive lineman Jahkeem Stewart was still on the injury report but is listed as probable. Stewart missed the first four games of the season after dealing with the same foot injury that hampered him last season. Linebacker Jadyn Walker is probable for Saturday's contest. Walker has been a key reserve this season behind Desman Stephens and Deven Bryant. Ta'Mere Robinson and Elijah Newby have also been key reserves this season. away.headline: L.J. Phillips injury update ahead of Iowa vs. Wisconsin football
away.blurb: Iowa will be trying to replace the production of Kamari Moulton, who is out for the season after suffering an injury against Minnesota . Moulton leads Iowa in carries (86), rushing yards (541) and rushing touchdowns (four) this season. Phillips ran for nearly 2,000 yards at FCS South Dakota last season and has the potential to provide serious firepower on the ground. But that hasn't materialized so far this season. He missed time due to injury earlier this season and has been limited to 25 carries for just 88 yards. His best game came against Washington, when he ran 10 times for 42 yards. Moulton's injury could also open the door for others like Braeden Jackson, Nathan McNeil and Xavier Williams. That trio went off against UNI, each rushing for at least 111 yards and combining for seven total touchdowns. But since then, Jackson, McNeil and Williams haven't contributed much on offense. Jackson provided an important spark on special teams with a kickoff return touchdown against Michigan, though. L.J. The Hawkeyes dropped to 5-2 after a 13-10 road loss to Minnesota on Saturday. It was a disappointing performance for an offense that looked like it had taken some major strides before the bye week. This loss showcased a lot of the faults in the offense. A poor running game and subpar quarterback play cost Iowa a winnable rivalry game. Kirk Ferentz and his team will now shift their attention to Wisconsin. The Badgers are riding high off a win over USC and playing some decent football at the moment. Iowa released its Week 9 depth chart on Monday. Running back Kamari Moulton departed the Minnesota game with an injury. Moulton isn't on the depth chart this week, and Ferentz revealed on Tuesday that the fourth-year back had suffered a season-ending injury. "Injury-wise, Kamari, he's going to be done for the season. So, unfortunately, he's going to be done. We'll look forward to getting him back here, but he's got some rehab to go through," Ferentz said on Tuesday. Iowa also listed its two quarterbacks, Hank Brown and Jeremy Hecklinski, with an "OR" distinction. But, Ferentz named Brown the starter on Tuesday. "Quarterback-wise, I think we listed Brown, Hecklinski, and plan to start Brown. We'll see how the week goes, but right now plan to start him and play it by ear from there," Ferentz said. Running back L.J. Phillips Jr. is also absent from this week's depth chart. Ferentz updated Phillips' status on Tuesday. "We'll see how it goes. He got to work a little bit today. That'll probably be day-to-day, so we'll see what the week brings there," Ferentz said of Phillips. It looks like Xavier Williams, Nathan McNeil, and Braeden Jackson could all see bigger workloads on Saturday. Iowa also listed its two quarterbacks, Hank Brown and Jeremy Hecklinski, with an "OR" distinction. But, Ferentz named Brown the starter on Tuesday. "Quarterback-wise, I think we listed Brown, Hecklinski, and plan to start Brown. We'll see how the week goes, but right now plan to start him and play it by ear from there," Ferentz said. Running back L.J. Phillips Jr. is also absent from this week's depth chart. Ferentz updated Phillips' status on Tuesday. "We'll see how it goes. He got to work a little bit today. picks.headline: Behind Enemy Lines: Auburn-Ole Miss preview with Sam Hutchens
picks.blurb: This week, we reached out to Sam Hutchens, the Ole Miss beat reporter for The Clarion-Ledger , for the inside scoop on Auburn's Week 9 opponent, the Ole Miss Rebels. This week's conversation with Hutchens focuses on the Rebels recent loss to Texas, the loss of a key player, former Tigers who are shining in Oxford, and much more. Here is this week's Behind Enemy Lines featuring Sam Hutchens of The Clarion-Ledger. What was your biggest takeaway from Ole Miss' recent loss to Texas? SH: "Ole Miss isn't good enough to dig itself out of huge holes. The Rebels were close to doing it in Austin, but Pete Golding was correct when he said they need to be more consistent." Kewan Lacy will not play on Saturday. What does the Ole Miss run game look like without him? SH: "There's a chance it's still pretty good. Makhi Frazier and JT Lindsey have been serviceable backups all year. Look for young Shekai Mills-Knight, who absolutely could be a future RB1 in the SEC, to get more carries too" A handful of former Tigers are with Ole Miss now, including Horatio Fields and Jay Crawford. How much impact have they made since joining the team? Do you expect either of them to dictate the outcome of Saturday's game? SH: "Both players have been solid transfer portal adds. Fields has been a little bit of an unexpected bright spot. He has the second-most catches on the team among receivers, behind Deuce Alexander. Going into the year, he wasn't the player many projected as the WR2." Which Tigers have your attention ahead of the game? SH: "Byrum Brown is the player I'm most excited to see. The Ole Miss rushing defense has been vulnerable at times this season, and the Rebels haven't generated pressure consistently. Maybe a recipe for Brown to shine." Ole Miss wins on Saturday if.... SH: "It turns the ball over one time or less. The Rebels are fantastic in home games over the past few seasons. They don't need a perfect game to win, but they must avoid self-inflicted errors." Taylor Jones is the lead writer for Auburn Wire, part of the USA TODAY Network. Follow him on X (formerly Twitter) and BlueSky . Follow Auburn Wire on X and Facebook .

away.headline: Early SEC availability report for Auburn's SEC game vs. LSU revealed
away.blurb: The initial SEC Student-Athlete Availability Report is out for this week's matchup between the Auburn Tigers and the No. 17 LSU Tigers at Jordan-Hare Stadium, and Auburn will enter the game with a relatively clean bill of health. Offensive lineman Tai Buster and tight end Hunter Herring remain "out" for Auburn, which has been the case since SEC play began in Week 3. However, one addition has been made. Defensive lineman Saint Farrior is listed as "questionable" for Saturday's game against LSU, meaning it is uncertain as of Wednesday whether he will be available to play. LSU will be without linebacker Will Weeks, safety Dashawn Speans, wide receiver Phillip Wright, and linebacker Charles Ross on Saturday, while defensive tackle Richard Anderson is listed as "doubtful." Wright is the most notable name on the report with three catches for 70 yards and a touchdown in LSU's season-opening win at Clemson. He has not played since Week 2 against Louisiana Tech. Linebacker Whit Weeks will miss his fourth straight game after he suffered a leg fracture in LSU's win over Texas A&M last month. Despite several players being out, LSU got good news Wednesday as wide receiver Jackson Harris, tight end Trey'Dez Green, and defensive end Princewill Umanmielen were left off the initial availability report and are expected to play this Saturday at Auburn. Harris leads LSU wide receivers with 456 yards and five touchdowns, and Green has 222 receiving yards and a touchdown this season. Umanmielen, who followed head coach Lane Kiffin from Ole Miss, leads the team in sacks with eight and is fourth in tackles with 27. Farrior played three snaps in Auburn's win over Georgia last week and has played in just four games this season for 17 total snaps. According to the SEC's website, "SEC school personnel must submit availability reports three days before each football game, with daily updates leading to a final report 90 minutes prior to game time." Inaccurate reports could result in fines between $25,000 and $100,000. Auburn will face LSU on Saturday at 11 a.m. CT. Taylor Jones is the lead writer for Auburn Wire, part of the USA TODAY Network. away.headline: Ole Miss vs. Auburn Injury Report: Jalyn Crawford, Terez Davis Questionable; Kewan Lacy Out
away.blurb: Ole Miss vs. Auburn Injury Report: Crawford, Davis Questionable WEDNESDAY Ole Miss vs. Auburn Injury Report: Crawford, Davis Questionable; Lacy Out ‘I've got to go out there and earn it’: Hunter Elliott returns with something to prove as Ole Miss opens fall OXFORD, Miss. – The first SEC availability report of Auburn week is out, and No. 12 Ole Miss has two key starters listed as questionable for Saturday. Cornerback Jalyn Crawford and left tackle Terez Davis are both questionable on the initial report, released at 7:10 p.m. CT on Wednesday. Running back Kewan Lacy is out, as expected, after dislocating his shoulder in last week's loss at Texas. Jalyn Crawford questionable after big night at Texas Pete Golding said Monday that Crawford “played his best game” at Texas and is “starting to show who we thought he was.” Losing him would be a big blow to a secondary that is already thin. Safety Edwin Joseph is out again as he works his way back from a procedure, and Golding said Monday he did not “feel great” about Joseph's chances this week. Safety MJ Preston, cornerback Cedrick Beavers, cornerback Iverson McCoy and safety Nascar McCoy are also out. Terez Davis questionable, but trending up Davis missed the Texas game after being a game-time decision, and he is questionable again to start the week. But Golding sounded confident Monday that his left tackle will be back. “Probably could have done it, but we didn't know what it was going to look like after and could have made it worse,” Golding said of holding Davis out in Austin. “So that's one definitely that we feel like, throughout this week, that we'll get back for this weekend.” Without Davis, Connor Howes moved to left tackle and Tommy Kinsler started at right tackle, and the line did not allow a sack. Howes and center Brycen Sanders are both listed as probable. Kewan Lacy out, Makhi Frazier steps in Ole Miss will also be without wide receivers Izaiah Hartrup and Kervin Johnson Jr., linebacker Ant Davis Jr. and offensive lineman Emanuel Faulkner. Defensive tackle Michai Boireau is probable. Auburn's list is short. Offensive lineman Tai Buster and tight end Hunter Herring are out, and wide receiver Jeremiah Koger is questionable. The SEC releases availability reports on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday evenings of game week, with a final update on game day. The Thursday report comes out at 7:10 p.m. CT, and the final report is due about 90 minutes before Saturday's 11:45 a.m. kickoff. With stadium renovations taking place in Jacksonville , the rivalry will be played in Atlanta this year. Both teams enter the game ranked for the first time since 2020, which is also the last time the Gators won it. UF (5-2, 3-2 in SEC) comes in hot after its second win over a top-10 team this season, a 27-24 victory at Texas . Backup quarterback Tramell Jones Jr. impressed with two touchdown passes and the game-sealing run, raising questions over whether he or Aaron Philo will get the start this week. Georgia (6-1, 4-1) fell from the ranks of the unbeaten two weeks ago when Byrum Brown spurred a late drive that led to Auburn's unbelievable 27-24 in Athens. Gunner Stockton threw for 272 yards and two score but also tossed a pair of interceptions, the second straight game in which he matched his TD and INT numbers. Buy Florida vs. Georgia football tickets Here's when the Gators and Bulldogs square off this week. Florida football schedule: UF's next game What time is UF vs UGA? The Gators and Bulldogs kick off at 3:30 p.m. on Saturday at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta. Florida vs Georgia prediction The Bulldogs have looked like the best team in the SEC all year and have numbers to show it: They rank first in the conference in both scoring offense (43 points per game) and defense (15.9 ppg). The obvious mismatch in this game comes through the air. UGA has a top-30 passing offense that has eight players with at least 100 yards receiving. UF fields a bottom-20 pass defense that allowed two straight embarrassing losses before the big Texas win. Florida has been able to counteract its deficiencies by getting to the quarterback, tying Georgia for third in the SEC with 22 sacks. UGA has protected Stockton well, though, allowing just eight sacks all year. picks.headline: ‘Florida's road win at Texas was very real' – ESPN's Greg McElroy predicts the final score of Florida vs Georgia
picks.blurb: ‘Florida's road win at Texas was very real' – ESPN's Greg McElroy predicts the final score of Florida vs Georgia - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Brewers win World Series NFL trade deadline proposals WNBA Finals schedule fiasco Anthony Edwards injury impact Week 8 fantasy trade tips Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Zach Ragan Tue, October 27, 2026 at 10:13 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Georgia Bulldogs and the Florida Gators will face off in Atlanta this weekend. The Georgia Bulldogs currently have a 71 percent chance to make the College Football Playoff, according to the A to Z Sports CFP predictor . If Georgia beats the Florida Gators on Saturday in Atlanta, the Bulldogs' chances of making the playoff jump to 83 percent. This won't be an easy task for Georgia. The Gators have been up and down this season. They looked dominant in a 52-28 win over Ole Miss before losing back-to-back games to Missouri and South Carolina. Then they bounced back with a win over Texas two weeks ago (the Gators were off last weekend). Florida isn't consistent, but they're dangerous. ESPN's Greg McElroy, though, has Georgia beating Florida by two scores. "Does Georgia's caution keep Florida around?" said McElroy while previewing this weekend's biggest games. "Look, Georgia goes for it less than any team in the FBS on fourth down, and they run fewer plays per game than most teams in the country. That's a formula for winning comfortably without covering a massive number because punts and field goals leave the door ajar, and if Georgia gets ahead early, then Smart will happily sit on it and try to pound away. "So here's what I'm thinking: these are the two biggest matchups in the game and they both belong to Georgia's offense. The short passing game against a defense that has struggled to stop it, and third down against a defense that has struggled to get off the field. Florida's road win at Texas was very real, but Georgia's front takes away the run game, and that's what made that upset possible. I'm taking Georgia to win the game 34-20. I think Florida did look really impressive on that road trip to Austin. They came home with a massive souvenir, but this is a different animal. Georgia now will be healthy coming out of the bye, and I think they've been excited about this opportunity to host this game in Atlanta." Georgia and Florida usually play in Jacksonville, but they're set to play in Atlanta this season (and in Tampa next season) due to renovations at EverBank Stadium. The SEC showdown moves from Jacksonville for the first time in decades, with significant postseason implications hanging in the balance. The Gators sit at No. 20 on the US LBM Coaches Poll , while the Bulldogs land at No. 3. Both teams entered their bye weeks under very different circumstances. Georgia surrendered its perfect record after being upset by Auburn and Florida knocked off Texas on the road to end a two-game skid. Under first-year head coach Jon Sumrall, the Gators have demonstrated an ability to compete with elite programs. However, inconsistency and sporadic lapses in execution paint question marks around UF's ceiling this season. Florida will need star running back Jadan Baugh to get going early to establish offensive balance and open up the play sheet for lead coordinator Buster Faulkner. Georgia boasts the No. 1 total defense in the SEC, so the Gators will need to stay out of predictable situations to maximize their weapons. The Gators' pass rush will need to recreate the pressure it delivered in Austin when the group sacked Arch Manning five times and forced two fumbles. Gunner Stockon turned the ball over three times against Auburn, so the opportunities should be there for Brad White's unit. Florida is again in the midst of a quarterback controversy. Aaron Philo led the Gators to a 4-0 start and was a driving force in their upset win over No. 4 Ole Miss in the Swamp before being sidelined by a right shoulder injury. In his first career start, Tramell Jones Jr. completed 22 of 35 passes for 155 yards and two touchdowns in a win over Texas that revived the Gators' season. Sumrall has yet to announce a starter as of Wednesday afternoon. Led by Gunner Stockton, Georgia's offense averages 43 points per game; a scoring attack that ranks No. 3 nationally. The unit also converts on 58% of its third-down attempts, which is among the most efficient in the nation. The Bulldogs have won five consecutive meetings, including last season's 24-20 battle. home.headline: Georgia’s new practice routine has made two Bulldogs’ injury status unknown
home.source: Dawn of the Dawg on MSN
home.blurb: Kirby Smart detailed on Monday how Georgia handled their bye week differently this season. In the past they have continued to practice like normal with limited time off, but this year they only practiced on Tuesday and Thursday and had the rest of the week off. "Really don't know on either one of them because we haven't done anything since Thursday,” Kirby Smart said via 247Sports.com . “Those guys, we had good practices all week last week, and then leading into this week, we'll find out more about where they are today and through the injury report information we have.” Smart made it clear that he is willing to sacrifice some practice time to get his team healthy. In fact, this is something that Georgia has been doing all season because they have shortened each of their practices all season by 10 or 15 minutes. The goal in this is to help Georgia stay healthier without giving up too much preparation time, and so far it has worked out alright. The hope though is that guys like Isiah Canion and KJ Bolden could use this extra time off this week to get healthy so they can make their return against Florida this weekend, but Smart hasn't confirmed if they will be back yet or not. The hope is that this would help get Georgia as healthy as possible going into the rest of the season, but according to Smart on Monday it still isn't clear if wide receiver Isiah Canion or defensive back KJ Bolden will be healthy enough to play against Florida this weekend. Georgia’s new practice routine will hopefully pay off Georgia is 6-1 so they could be better off this season, but their record is still good enough to be the No. 3 team in the country. UGA has also had to deal with a handful of injuries throughout the season, but if you compare their injury report to other teams across the country they have had less injuries than others. Georgia desperately needs KJ Bolden back Georgia has only been without KJ Bolden for one game this season, and it just so happened to be their worst game of the year. UGA was without Bolden when they played Auburn two weeks ago and they were upset at home as the No. 1 team in the country. Who knows if Bolden could've changed that outcome if he was in the game, but it might not be a coincidence that Georgia's defense had their worst game of the season when he wasn't able to play. Georgia has been without Canion for longer, so they've already learned how to get by without him on offense. The same can't be said for Bolden though who is a projected first round pick at the upcoming NFL Draft this offseason. If Georgia wants their best shot at avoiding another upset they need Bolden back in the lineup to help slow down a Florida offense who is capable of scoring a lot of points. picks.headline: 4 bold predictions as Oregon football takes on Northwestern
picks.blurb: News Sports Entertainment Life Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL 4 bold predictions as Oregon football takes on Northwestern Alec Dietz Eugene Register-Guard Oct. 28, 2026, 8:52 a.m. PT Oregon's national-title hopes have ended after a loss to Illinois dropped them to 4-3. Oregon will face a one-loss Northwestern team featuring former Ducks coach Chip Kelly as offensive coordinator. The Ducks' defense is expected to play well, but the offense faces a tough challenge against Northwestern. The Oregon football team's national title hopes are all but over, and it isn't even November. After entering the season ranked as high as they've ever been, the Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) are unranked and out of the immediate College Football Playoff race after a stunning loss to Illinois on the road . The Ducks don't have much time to lick their wounds, either. After firing offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer and announcing quarterback Dante Moore will miss the rest of the 2026 season , one-loss Northwestern comes to town . Chip Kelly, who guided Oregon to a national championship game appearance as head coach over a decade ago, is the Wildcats' offensive coordinator. "It's almost like you're playing three different offenses," Oregon coach Dan Lanning said of Northwestern. "The new wrinkles that (Kelly) has at Northwestern, some of the old flavor that he has that he's carried all the way to his time back here at Oregon. There's always going to be something new when you walk into a game that it's going to be like he's never put this on film. He might not know how you're going to line up against it, and you have to figure it out there within the rules of your defense and how you execute." Oregon vs. Northwestern scouting report Why Oregon has an advantage: The Ducks will have the home crowd behind them in Eugene and also have deep familiarity with Northwestern's starting quarterback, Aidan Chiles. The senior signal-caller started his career at Oregon State before transferring to Michigan State in 2024. Chiles played at Autzen Stadium in that year and had a rough outing, completely just 10 of 17 passes for 154 yards in a 31-10 loss. The Ducks found ways to rattle Chiles early, and with a strong pass rush in recent weeks they could do so again Saturday. Why Northwestern has an advantage: The Wildcats, under first-year offensive coordinator and former Ducks coach Chip Kelly, have one of the most efficient offenses in the country and don't make many mistakes. Northwestern isn't necessarily an offensive juggernaut, but it ranks fifth in the country in turnover margin and moves the ball methodically while keeping opposing teams out of the end zone defensively. Though the Wildcats' defense gives up plenty of yards, they rank in the top 25 in scoring defense allowing just 16.6 points per game. Oregon vs. Northwestern injury updates Note: Official availability reports, mandated by the Big Ten, are released every day starting at 5 p.m. Wednesday leading up to kickoff. This story was published before the reports were made public. For Oregon: The Ducks will have a good chunk of playmakers returning to the sideline this weekend after sitting out last week due to unknown reasons. Evan Stewart, who was out last week after a DUII arrest, is expected back, as are Jalen Lott and Messiah Hampton. Lanning did not elaborate why Hampton and Lott missed last week. The coach also announced quarterback Dante Moore will likely miss the rest of the 2026 season after sustaining a concussion in late September. For Northwestern: The Wildcats were without several key contributors last week in a win against Rutgers, especially defensively. Second-leading tackler Robert Fitzgerald was held out, as well as defensive lineman Brendan Flakes. Oregon vs. Northwestern: 4 bold predictions Ducks will mostly contain vaunted Northwestern run game Though Chiles has been successful through the air in recent weeks, Northwestern's bread and butter is establishing the ground game. After a subpar performance stopping the run last week against Illinois, Oregon's defense will show up ready to play and stifle backs Caleb Komolafe, Joseph Himon II and Gavin Sawchuk. Outside of games versus Oklahoma State and Illinois, Oregon's run defense has been sound and it'll look like a motivated group against a physical Wildcats team this weekend. Gage Hurych will have a bounce-back performance vs. Wildcats After missing three field goals last week in a loss to Illinois, all from 40 yards or more, junior kicker Gage Hurych will have a strong game against Northwestern. The Wildcats give up a lot of yards with a bend-but-don't-break defense but are elite in the red zone, an area where Oregon's offense struggles. Northwestern opponents only score a touchdown on 40% of possessions that reach the red zone. If Oregon's offense stalls as it gets closer to the end zone, look for Hurych to have a bounce-back performance with more manageable field-goal attempts. Ducks' defense will keep them in it until the end Though Oregon's offense will likely still have trouble after firing Drew Mehringer, its defense will respond and keep them in the game until the fourth quarter. Outside of a couple of broken off runs in a loss to Illinois, the Ducks' defense has been one of the top units in the country over the last month and that will continue against Northwestern this weekend. It just won't be enough to get a win, unless the offense really corrects itself. picks.headline: Northwestern is up next for Oregon football. A sneak preview
picks.blurb: News Sports Entertainment Life Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL Northwestern is up next for Oregon football. A sneak preview Chris Hansen Eugene Register-Guard Oct. 26, 2026, 5:14 a.m. PT The Oregon Ducks will host the No. 18 Northwestern Wildcats on Saturday, October 31. Northwestern's offense is led by former Oregon head coach Chip Kelly, who is now the offensive coordinator. Northwestern quarterback Aidan Chiles is having a career-best season under Kelly's guidance. No time to wallow for Oregon's coaches and players. There's still lots of football left and against some pretty good teams. That includes this coming weekend. The Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten Conference) will host No. 18 Northwestern (6-1, 3-1) and former Oregon head coach Chip Kelly at 12:30 p.m. Oct. 31. Kelly, who is in his first season as offensive coordinator on coach David Braun's staff, has the Wildcats humming. They are third in the Big Ten in total yards per game (435.6) and points (34.7) and are No. 2 in rushing yards per game (204.6). Northwestern is coming off a 42-14 win against Rutgers, the fourth straight win for the Wildcats since a 29-23 loss to Indiana on Sept. 25. The Ducks are coming off a 21-10 loss to Illinois that, barring a miracle, has ended their shot at making the College Football Playoff for a third straight season. On Sunday, Oregon fired first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . Here's an early look at Northwestern. Who is the Northwestern QB? The Wildcats have a familiar face at quarterback in Aidan Chiles, who previously played at Oregon State and Michigan State. The 6-foot-4, 225-pound dual-threat senior has been unlocked by Kelly and is having the best season of his career. Chiles has completed 117 of 164 passes for 1,617 yards and has 12 touchdowns to one interception. He's also rushed for a team-leading nine touchdowns. Last week against Rutgers he completed 19 of 25 passes for 219 yards and three touchdowns and rushed for 83 yards and two touchdowns. He is the only player in the country to have multiple games of at least three passing touchdowns and two rushing touchdowns this season. Other Northwestern offensive standouts Junior wide receiver Griffin Wilde has 39 catches for 615 yards and four touchdowns. In the game against Rutgers on Saturday, he had nine receptions for 133 yards and a touchdown. Running back Caleb Komolafe leads the Wildcats in rushing with 551 yards and five touchdowns on 88 carries. He also had a big game against Rutgers, rushing for 150 yards and a touchdown on just 13 carries (11.5 yards per run). Joseph Himon II has been productive as well. He has 371 yards and three scores on 38 carries with an average of 9.8 yards per run. Defensive standouts for Northwestern Fifth-year Braydon Brus has been disruptive from his linebacker position, leading the team with 62 tackles, 11.0 tackles for loss and four sacks. He also has an interception and a fumble recovery. He is the conference co-leader in tackles and No. 2 in TFLs. Safety Robert Fitzgerald, a second-team all-conference player in 2025, is second on the team with 49 tackles and has a team-leading two interceptions, though he has missed the last two games with an injury. Fitzgerald’s 9.0 tackles per game leads the Big Ten. The last time the Ducks and Wildcats met Oregon and Northwestern have played each other just two times, and never before at Autzen Stadium. The Wildcats beat the Ducks in Evanston, Ill., in 1974, and last season Oregon came out on top 34-14. Dante Moore was 16-of-20 passing for 178 yards and a touchdown, and Dierre Hill Jr. had a 66-yard touchdown run in the third quarter as the Ducks built a 31-0 lead. All of Northwestern's points came in the fourth quarter after the Ducks pulled most of their starters. home.blurb: With quarterback Dante Moore as well as wide receivers Evan Stewart and Jeremiah McClellan all listed "Out" on Oregon's first availability report released on Wednesday, the passing offense may look a bit different for the Ducks against Illinois. How the Illinois game plays out remains to be seen, but the Ducks likely can't afford to lose another game and keep their College Football Playoff hopes alive. Oregon Ducks coach Dan Lanning has been open about the 2026 season's challenges and how they have forced him to grow, and struggles on the offensive side of the ball remain a continued point of discussion. In the 17-14 win over Nebraska, receiver Dakorien Moore logged 14 targets and seven receptions as the Ducks' leading receiver. Moore can be expected to lead the receiver room again on Saturday vs. the Fighting Illini, but younger receivers like Messiah Hampton, Jalen Lott, and Gatlin Bair could see their respective roles increase. After Wednesday's practice, Lanning spoke about coordinating the passing game with a group of younger receivers, first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer, and backup quarterbacks in Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Dan Lanning on Oregon Ducks Passing Game Lanning stressed keeping Oregon’s offense simple as injuries mount, giving younger players a chance to master the fundamentals and make plays. “Yeah, I think you got to go back to your roots of, like, what is our system? What's that look like? What's you got to make it simple for players rather than you know packaging multiple things. Maybe this is a good answer versus multiple coverages, right?" Lanning said. “And ask our guys to be able to execute that at a high level, hold the standard higher, right? Are we finishing in a dominant position? Are we blocking on the perimeter the way we need to? Are we attacking the ball and really coach the fundamentals?” “I think a lot of people start to coach scheme more in those moments, and then again, an awareness of your team, recognize your strengths, be able to play into that," the Oregon coach continued. "And that doesn't always mean – sometimes the best third-down play is an opportunity to still have the ball and punt it away, right?” “Because the reality is, you get an opportunity to flip the field for a large sum of yards. Sometimes the best red-area play is burning the ball as a quarterback, so you get a chance to kick a field goal. There's, it's all about making sure we have opportunities to have points and make great decisions. But we have good players. And those guys have given them an opportunity to step up and make plays.” Oregon's Quarterback Situation vs. Illinois Lanning and the Ducks have not made an announcement as to which quarterback will start on Saturday against Illinois, but some signs point to Raiola getting the nod with the Nebraska transfer also speaking to the media on Wednesday. home.blurb: After narrowly escaping East Lansing, Michigan, with a 38-37 overtime victory almost two weeks ago, Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) will return home Saturday (2 p.m. CT, Big Ten Network) to face Oregon (4-2, 2-1 Big Ten). The Illini entered their bye week with a little momentum and, more importantly, a season that wasn't completely dead yet. Unfortunately, their reward for keeping the season alive is a date with one of college football's premier programs. The good news for Illinois: Oregon hasn't exactly been the unstoppable machine many expected, either. Under coach Dan Lanning, the Ducks have established themselves as one of the nation's elite programs. Oregon entered 2026 with College Football Playoff aspirations, but things haven't gone quite according to plan. Oregon opened with a 34-27 victory over Boise State before suffering a surprising 39-31 loss at Oklahoma State. After demolishing Portland State 84-0, the Ducks picked up an impressive 41-27 road victory over USC. Since then, however, things have gotten more interesting – or harrowing, depending on your perspective. Oregon suffered a 17-15 home loss to UCLA before barely escaping Nebraska with a 17-14 victory last Saturday. The Ducks needed a touchdown with just seconds remaining to avoid another embarrassing home defeat. Suddenly, a team expected to compete for a national championship is loping along at 4-2 and fighting to keep its playoff hopes alive. Of course, for Illinois fans, a disappointing Oregon season probably sounds pretty appealing right about now. Oregon's offense has been dangerous under Lanning, but injuries at quarterback have created plenty of uncertainty. Starter Dante Moore threw for 926 yards and nine touchdowns without an interception before suffering a concussion against USC. Since then, Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas have both seen action, with neither able to consistently replicate Moore's production. Despite the uncertainty at quarterback, Oregon still has plenty of weapons. Running back Jordon Davison leads the Ducks with 330 rushing yards and six touchdowns, while Dierre Hill Jr. has added 295 yards and three scores. At receiver, Evan Stewart leads the team with 352 receiving yards, while Dakorien Moore has recorded 347 yards and four touchdowns. Although Oregon's offense has struggled in recent weeks, the Ducks still possess more than enough talent to give Illinois' struggling defense plenty of problems. Unlike its offense, Oregon's defense has remained relatively consistent. The Ducks are allowing just 20.7 points and 327.3 total yards per game, while holding opponents to only 111.7 rushing yards per game. Leading the way is a talented defensive front featuring Matayo Uiagalelei and Teitum Tuioti. Uiagalelei has recorded 24.5 career sacks, while Tuioti added two sacks and 2.5 tackles for loss against Nebraska last weekend. But he showed off his freakish athleticism Saturday against the Volunteers with one of the most impressive 4-yard gains for a touchdown you'll see. Wide receiver Nyck Harbor is a big-play threat at any moment. Defensively, Dylan Stewart wreaks havoc on most offenses he faces — he's recorded two sacks and forced three fumbles in four games this season. The case for South Carolina: Beamer has the Gamecocks rolling. Momentum can be a real thing. If Sellers limits his turnovers and South Carolina's defense forces OU quarterback John Mateer, it'll have a good chance on the road. Mateer wasn't sensational but he didn't have to be. With an elite defense, OU just needs Mateer to play smart, turnover-free football. Oklahoma vs. South Carolina: Initial injury report for Week 9
away.blurb: On offense, key players like Ryan Fodje and Eddy Pierre-Louis aren't close to returning and were ruled out for this week. However, guard Heath Ozaeta could make his first appearance since the win over Texas. Ozaeta was listed as probable. If he's able to play, that provides Oklahoma a valuable piece to their interior offensive line rotation. If he's able to play, it's likely Ozaeta slides back into the starting lineup, but could platoon with Peyton Joseph, who has had some ups and downs for the Sooners over the last two weeks. It also looks like running back Xavier Robinson could be available this week. The Carl Albert product hasn't played since the Week 4 loss to Georgia and saw fewer than 10 snaps in back-to-back weeks before suffering a calf strain. He'll battle with Jonathan Hatton for the third running back carries as Lloyd Avant and Tory Blaylock have established themselves as the Sooners' 1-2 punch in the running back rotation. Defensively, the Oklahoma Sooners have big questions. Rotational linebacker Cole Sullivan was ruled out for this week. Safety Peyton Bowen and cornerback Eli Bowen are both questionable for Week 9. Both Bowens are key pieces to the Sooners' defense, and against a good South Carolina passing attack, Peyton's presence is critical. He's one of the best safeties in college football. If he can't play, it'll be Omarion Robinson and Michael Boganowski starting at the safety spots, and potentially Reggie Powers mixing into the rotation. If Eli is out, Trystan Haynes would likely get another start. Wide receiver Parker Livingstone and running back Tory Blaylock were moved to probable ahead of Saturday's matchup with Mississippi State . picks.blurb: Clemson (4-3, 3-2 ACC) is coming off a last-minute 20-16 loss to the Virginia Tech Hokies at Memorial Stadium. The Tigers led for much of the second half, but Hokies quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer led his team on an 11-play, 69-yard drive for the game-winning score with 1:44 to play. Grunkmeyer's 5-yard touchdown pass to tight end Luke Reynolds on fourth-and-1 gave Virginia Tech its first win over Clemson in 19 years and dropped the Tigers to 2-8 in their last 10 home games against Power Four opponents. The offense struggled once again, netting only 288 total yards and going 3 of 14 on third downs. Freshman QB Tait Reynolds completed 20 of his 26 passes, but his average completion went for only 5.9 yards. The Tigers rank dead last in the ACC and just 115th nationally in total offense with 333.1 yards per game. Clemson will face a Florida State (3-4, 1-3) team fresh off a bye, and one that should be playing with plenty of confidence. Mike Norvell's Seminoles took the top-ranked Miami Hurricanes into double overtime before falling 43-35 at Hard Rock Stadium on Oct. 17. Fifth-year senior Ashton Daniels leads the Seminoles' passing attack and has 1,618 yards and 12 touchdowns to eight interceptions in seven games this season. Daniels threw four touchdown passes and rushed for another score in FSU's loss to Miami in Week 7. Clemson has won nine of the last 10 meetings against Florida State dating back to 2015. Will the Tigers' run of dominance in the rivalry continue or end Saturday in Tallahassee? Will Clemson football beat Florida State? ESPN's prediction Oddsmakers have Florida State as a 6.5-point favorite over Clemson, but as always, ESPN Analytics has its own odds for Saturday's game. ESPN's matchup predictor , which offers a prediction model based on its college football power index and other variables, doesn't favor the Tigers, either. It gives Florida State a 71.9% chance to win and Clemson a 28.1% chance. The Tigers are 51st nationally in ESPN's FPI with a 5.8 rating, which ranks 11th among the 17 ACC teams. Florida State has a 10.1 FPI rating that's 37th nationally. The Tigers are one spot ahead of Kansas State (5.7) and one spot below Virginia (6.0). away.headline: DT Vic Burley added to injury report for Clemson vs Virginia Tech
away.blurb: Burley, a senior, was listed as questionable again after being added Oct. 22. He was not listed on the initial report Oct. 21. Burley has played in four games after missing the first two because of a suspension. He got his first tackle, a sack, in Week 7 vs Georgia Southern. Clemson wide receiver Gordon Sellars III is listed as out. Tigers coach Dabo Swinney said that Sellars has a concussion and is going through concussion protocol. He's made three catches for 8 yards in a backup role. Defensive tackle Devarrick Woods and running back Jarvis Green don't appear on the injury report for Clemson. Swinney has said that he expects both players to return from injury against Virginia Tech. Vizzina was removed from the Tigers' injury report against California on Sept. 25 ahead of kickoff that night and hasn't appeared once since. However, Vizzina hasn't fully recovered, and he was only available for emergencies against Miami and Charleston Southern. Vizzina has been recovering from a small fracture in his left elbow after originally injuring it against Georgia Southern on Sept. 12. Swinney said after the Charleston Southern game that he wouldn't have had an issue with playing Vizzina against the Buccaneers, but that Vizzina told him he wasn't ready and that Brock Bradley should enter instead. home.blurb: Florida State coach Mike Norvell recently provided a couple of injury updates on multiple Seminoles who have missed significant time this season. Injuries have been a huge issue for the team this year for Norvell, particularly on defense, where multiple players are out for the season. Sometimes injuries can make or break a team, and so far, the Seminoles have been able to do quite a bit with multiple contributors sidelined. Norvell kicked off his injury updates portion of the press conference with a quick tidbit on linebacker Blake Nichelson, who has not played since the season opener against New Mexico State. Nichelson is nearing a return, and while the game against Clemson might still be out of reach , the linebacker should be able to return to play soon. Samuel Singleton Jr.'s return would be huge for the Florida State offense Norvell is not giving up on Singleton's return; he never ruled the running back out for the season, and he clearly still thinks there is hope for his return. It might be a delusion at this point from Norvell to avoid the reality that Florida State is in a bad spot at running back, or a future return this season might still truly be in the cards. I personally would like to think that Singleton is close to coming back, and the faster he can return, the better for Florida State. Tre Wisner is an experienced running back, but he has not been the most effective player in a short sample size this season. Aside from Wisner, there is not much of an experienced supporting cast. Additionally, Florida State might be in trouble if Singleton is not able to return this season due to the fact that there are only three healthy running backs. The Seminoles truly cannot afford to have another running back go down with an injury, and if Singleton is not available for another two or three weeks, that could be an issue. The timing of Crutchfield's return could not be any better, with Quindarrius Jones, Nehemiah Chandler, and Ashlynd Barker all dealing with injuries. Barker has been playing through his injury thanks to a cast, but Crutchfield can do it all in the secondary, and he should be able to take some pressure off multiple players. Norvell revealed that senior linebacker Blake Nichelson is "progressing" but likely still would not be able to return to play just yet. With Clemson coming to Tallahassee on October 31, Nichelson may need more time to properly rehab his injury. The linebacker recorded three total tackles against New Mexico State in the season opener in Tallahassee before going down with an injury. Nichelson has not seen the field since, but a return during the season has never been ruled out. Florida State could greatly benefit from a Blake Nichelson return this season Both for Nichelson and Florida State, returning to the field this season would be extremely beneficial, given the struggles the team has had. The Seminoles are down so many players at some positions that some players are playing significantly more than the staff would like. Nichelson gives the rest of the linebackers a chance to breathe, and he offers the staff a veteran presence that can help the defense work out some of the communication issues present. Florida State is right back into game mode after receiving a bye in Week 8 to recuperate for the final five games of the 2026 season. The year has been far from what the fans had hoped for, but unfortunately, it has been eerily similar to what many experts felt it would be. Once again, the Seminoles are in an awkward position as the light that comes with winning is slowly fading away. For the Seminoles, virtually the entire roster has been hit with injuries at one point or another this season, and some positions took big hits. The secondary has been running with nearly no depth due to the number of injuries, and other positions have been playing without key players for most of the season. At linebacker, Nichelson was expected to take another step forward this season for Florida State, with a bigger role on defense. However, Nichelson's injury forced the Seminoles' staff to move things around, and nearly every linebacker has been included in an injury report this season. The Seminoles need to get healthy to be more competitive this season, and getting Nichelson back would be a huge boost defensively. Nichelson has been a Florida State mainstay the past few seasons , with 115 total tackles since the 2023 season. That extra point on the spread matters, and I wouldn't pretend every sportsbook is still offering it. This is an outdoor game, so I'll want another look at the Chapel Hill weather forecast before kickoff, particularly the wind and any chance of rain. Miami Hurricanes Have the Offense to Put This Away Early Miami is 7-0, including 3-0 away from home, and just beat Pittsburgh 52-23. The Hurricanes have scored 43 or more in three of their last four games, and they've already beaten Clemson 41-13 on the road. That's a pretty good argument for laying the points, I'll give you that. Pittsburgh couldn't do much with Miami's passing game Saturday. The Hurricanes scored 52, and the scary part is that they still left some plays out there. North Carolina isn't going to survive if it spends the first half giving Miami short fields and easy touchdowns. The numbers explain why the Hurricanes are such a big favorite. They're averaging 49 points and 552 yards per game. Nobody in the country is producing more total offense. Miami throws for about 341 yards a game and runs for another 211, so taking away one part of the offense doesn't necessarily solve anything. Defensively, the Hurricanes allow just 15.3 points and 60 rushing yards per game. Sixty. That's going to make life difficult for a North Carolina offense that hasn't run the ball particularly well. Miami also converts 54.5% of its third downs. If the Tar Heels can't get the Hurricanes off the field, that home crowd won't have much to cheer about. Malachi Toney caught 16 passes for 194 yards and three touchdowns in that game, giving him 952 receiving yards and 11 touchdowns on the season. Javian Mallory has added 444 rushing yards and seven touchdowns. That's plenty of offense for North Carolina to worry about. Miami does have some injuries, with receiver Jalen Moore and running back Chris Brown out for the season. Tight end Logan Gilbert is also sidelined, while Owen Ruskavich's status needs checking. But the Hurricanes haven't had much trouble scoring without them. North Carolina Tar Heels Need to Make Miami Earn Everything North Carolina is 4-3 overall and 1-2 at home. The Tar Heels had won two straight before losing 31-30 to Syracuse in overtime Saturday. That one had to sting. They had a chance to get their fifth win and instead let Syracuse walk out of Chapel Hill with it. Still, I wouldn't throw out everything North Carolina has done because of one ugly finish. The Tar Heels beat Pittsburgh 21-17 on the road and followed it with a 24-20 win at Duke. They also played Clemson to an eight-point game. Those aren't the results of a team that rolls over every time it sees a better opponent. The offense is the problem. North Carolina averages 24.4 points and 336 yards per game, and the running game produces only 114 yards a night. That's not much help against Miami's defensive front. The Tar Heels are probably going to have to throw more than they'd like. Defensively, though, they've allowed 20.9 points per game. That's respectable, even if the 373 yards they're giving up tells you opponents are moving the ball. What worries me most is third down. North Carolina allows opponents to convert 43.1% of the time. Miami is one of the best third-down teams in the country. That's a bad matchup, and Bill Belichick has to find a way to get his defense off the field before the Hurricanes start piling up possessions. Billy Edwards Jr. has thrown for 1,530 yards with 11 touchdowns and five interceptions. He passed for 271 yards and two scores against Syracuse, so he can move the ball when he gets protection. Jordan Shipp has 543 receiving yards, including eight catches for 102 yards and a touchdown Saturday. Benjamin Hall leads the running backs with 283 yards, while Demon June has seven rushing touchdowns. The Tar Heels are dealing with some injuries at receiver, including Carnell Warren and Kaden Chapman, and they're missing tight ends Jordan Washington and Jake Warren. That's not ideal when you're facing a defense as good as Miami's. But Edwards has enough experience to keep North Carolina from becoming completely one-dimensional. I know Miami could make this look foolish in a hurry. The Hurricanes have the better quarterback, the better offense and a defense that barely lets anybody run the ball. But sixteen and a half points is a lot to lay on the road against a team that's been competitive with Clemson, Pittsburgh and Duke. North Carolina has lost three games, and two of those defeats came by eight points or fewer. The Tar Heels also have a quarterback who can throw well enough to put together a late scoring drive if they're down a couple of touchdowns. That's what I'm looking for here. Miami can control most of the game and still fail to cover a number this big. I wouldn't be surprised by a 30-17 or 34-20 Miami win. Either one gets the job done for North Carolina backers at +16.5. At +14.5, though, I like it considerably less. I'll take Under 51.5, although this is the pick that makes me a little nervous. Miami is averaging 49 points a game by itself, and that's not something you can just ignore. But North Carolina isn't built to get into a scoring contest with the Hurricanes. The Tar Heels need to run some clock, avoid turnovers and make Miami work for its points. They can't afford to turn this into a game where both teams are snapping the ball every twenty seconds. Miami's defense should help us here because the Hurricanes allow only 15.3 points per game and have been excellent against the run. If North Carolina finishes somewhere around 14 or 17 points, Miami can score into the low 30s without pushing this over. The danger is an early Miami explosion or a couple of defensive touchdowns. That's real. But I think the Tar Heels will try to slow the game down, and Miami's defense should keep North Carolina from doing too much scoring. Give me Miami 31-17. away.headline: Notre Dame can survive its latest injury wave against Navy, but Miami is different
away.blurb: Notre Dame football’s “ next man up ” philosophy should be enough to get Marcus Freeman through Navy despite another crowded injury report. But with DJ McKinney out, Brauntae Johnson still sidelined, and Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa among the questionable players, Chris Ash needs that list to shrink considerably before Miami arrives. Despite the Fighting Irish coming off a bye week , head coach Marcus Freeman detailed several injuries that will hit Chris Ash’s unit hard. The good news is that none of the players who will miss time or be questionable are ones the team should need against Navy. The question is how healthy some of these guys will be in two weeks against Miami. On Monday afternoon, Freeman said McKinney is out for the Navy game with an ankle injury. That’s never good news, as that kind of injury can stick around for a while. A cornerback who can’t make cuts won’t keep up with receivers. That’s not an issue against Navy, but against Miami, especially Malachi Toney, it’s a big one. Another big injury update: safety Brauntae Johnson is still out. Notre Dame has hoped he’d be out for “just a couple of weeks” after he was injured in the first half of the season opener. However, with the season now in Week 8, people have to start worrying about whether he will play this year. The injury list doesn’t end there. Freeman said that tight end Cooper Flanagan (hamstring), linebacker Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa (thumb), defensive lineman Loghan Thomas (shoulder), and cornerback Mark Zackery IV (concussion) are all questionable. Of course, of all the injuries that might just be cautionary, KVA’s questionable status is the most likely situation where he could have been fine to play if Miami was this week. Notre Dame should absolutely be able to beat Navy even without Viliamu-Asa in the lineup. The injury that should make Notre Dame faithful most worried is DJ McKinney’s. The transfer cornerback was hurt late in the game against BYU , and the bye week apparently wasn't enough time for him to heal and get back to 100%. Notre Dame football defensive injuries create bigger questions for Miami than Navy Because Notre Dame knows Navy won’t tax its cornerbacks much, sitting McKinney this week isn’t a shock. It’s even possible that if this were Miami week , they’d be working to get him back on the field. The Irish won’t push it against the Midshipmen. The most interesting note in that group is that Notre Dame took quite a bit of heat for not playing Viliamu-Asa more against BYU. It’s clear now that one reason he wasn’t in the game more was that his thumb was still bothering him.
