This feels like 2007 all over again, thanks to the pure chaos that has ensued over the last two weeks within the top 25. At this point, we're not expecting anything less on Halloween in Week 9, despite only two matchups pitting nationally ranked teams -- the SEC's Georgia vs. Florida showdown from Atlanta and Arizona vs. Texas Tech in the topsy-turvy Big 12. Only three unbeatens in the Power Four remain as the season approaches its final month, with the first CFP rankings set to debut in less than a week. We hope you're betting responsibly this fall, considering this parity-rich party nationwide that shows no signs of ceasing. Season results : Brad Crawford (47-24 straight up, 35-35-1 ATS); Chris Hummer (51-20 straight up, 38–32-1 ATS) My colleague's hot streak continues. After tying things up at midseason against the spread, Hummer's sizzling Week 8 effort has pushed him out front. It's quite humbling for yours truly, whose multi-year reign atop the picks mountain is in serious jeopardy. Perhaps Saturday afternoon comes up aces for me, and we enter November tied again after a rally. On the flip side, Hummer's could swell. No. 25 Wisconsin at Iowa (-3.5) Hummer ( Wisconsin +3.5) : These two teams do the same things well: Run the ball, stop the run. The Hawkeyes are a better rushing offense, while Wisconsin, with Colton Joseph , has the more dynamic option at quarterback -- he uses his legs a lot. To me, this game comes down to which team can avoid turnovers. They've been a killer in losses for Iowa this season. Iowa avoids those against the Badgers and wins a classic Big Ten slugfest at home. The Badgers cover, though. … Iowa 20, Wisconsin 17. Crawford (Wisconsin +3.5) : Had a feeling the Badgers would be ranked at some point this season after watching the opener against Notre Dame . The operation just looked more fluid, despite the final score in a matchup that was more competitive than the final outcome. I believe oddsmakers are giving too much respect to the Hawkeyes here playing at home. An outright win could move the Badgers inside the top 20 of the CFP selection committee's first rankings next week. I'll go ahead and take this one as my upset special in Week 9. ... Wisconsin 23, Iowa 20. No. 22 Arizona at No. 13 Texas Tech (-5.5) Hummer (Texas Tech -5.5 ): A critical matchup in the Big 12 race, the Red Raiders are facing their toughest test since Houston in Week 2. The Wildcats have put up points in bunches this season. But I will say the one week the Wildcats struggled was against BYU , when their run game was bottled up by BYU's defensive front. That's a major potential advantage for Texas Tech in this matchup. The Red Raiders are an excellent front seven and should win that matchup. Can Texas Tech score enough to win this one? It's been a struggle at times, but they get it done. … Texas Tech 27, Arizona 20. Crawford (Texas Tech -5.5) : This is the week we'll be talking about the Wildcats nationally if Arizona finds a way to beat Texas Tech in Lubbock. I don't think it happens, however. The Red Raiders' backs are against the wall in this spot, knowing another loss tanks any shot at reaching the CFP -- or even getting back to the Big 12 title game as the defending league champions. Will Hammond does not have a multi-touchdown outing this season as a passer, but this could be the weekend it finally happens at home. I trust Texas Tech more in this spot than Arizona. ... Texas Tech 31, Arizona 24. Auburn at No. 12 Ole Miss (-12.5) Hummer ( Auburn +12.5): Auburn has struggled this year against above-average defensive fronts. The Rebels aren't elite in that area, but they do blitz a ton and create a lot of havoc around the line of scrimmage. It's going to be up to Byrum Brown to pick up those blitzes and extend plays with his feet. Even without Kewan Lacy , Trinidad Chambliss allows them to score enough. The question is whether Auburn can keep up. I think the Tigers do enough to cover. … Ole Miss 34, Auburn 24. Crawford (Auburn +12.5) : Life in the SEC is hard. Auburn goes from beating Georgia in Athens one week to getting housed on The Plains by another nationally ranked foe the next. Rinse, repeat. If the Tigers had trouble defending Sam Leavitt and that LSU offense, they're going to have equally as much trouble this weekend in Oxford against Trinidad Chambliss. We've seemed to have dismissed his Heisman hopes after the loss at Texas , and that's unwise. Ole Miss gets Georgia coming up, and there are several more opportunities to shine, including this one. I do still have questions about this Ole Miss defense, however. ... Ole Miss 38, Auburn 27. Minnesota at No. 4 Indiana (-20.5) Hummer ( Minnesota +20.5) : That feels like an aggressive line based on what we've seen from Indiana 's offense of late, right? The Gophers are a top-30 defense in terms of yards allowed per play and should be able to challenge Indiana the way Nebraska , Ohio State and Michigan have in recent weeks. The question becomes, can Minnesota score enough to make this a game? The Gophers are 118th nationally in yards per play and have only scored more than 21 points against Power Four competition once this season. It's going to be tough for Minnesota to manufacture points, but the Gophers do enough. … Indiana 27, Minnesota 10. Crawford (Minnesota +20.5) : Can Indiana cover a three-touchdown spread? I have my doubts with Josh Hoover back there. Maybe this is the week the Hoosiers figure it out in the passing game, but the Gophers are sound on the back end and aren't likely to give up explosive plays. I've moved off Indiana in the elite tier of playoff contenders, but the Hoosiers should win here and be ranked inside the top 5 in next week's first CFP rankings. ... Indiana 31, Minnesota 17 . No. 17 Florida vs. No. 3 Georgia (-10.5) Hummer (Florida +10.5) : Was Florida's defensive performance against Texas an aberration or the new norm? That's the big question entering this game. The Gators are 121st nationally in passing yards per game, and the Bulldogs are a top-30 passing offense. That should be a big advantage for UGA. But that unit largely held Texas in check. Otherwise, this is a reasonably even matchup across the board. Georgia's O-line is better -- yes. Florida matches up well otherwise. Georgia wins this game coming off the bye week. But I do like the Gators to stay in this one for 60 minutes. … Georgia 34, Florida 27. Crawford (Georgia -10.5) : One of college football's most difficult teams to predict this season, I'm 0-2 picking the Gators against the spread after the loss to South Carolina and subsequent rally at Texas. I've given up trying to figure out which Florida team shows up week to week since that 4-0 start in September pushed the Gators to No. 8 in the AP poll. A victory in Atlanta puts Jon Sumrall's squad back in the CFP discussion near the top of the SEC and threatens Georgia's reign in the league standings. What's more likely, however, is Gunner Stockton recovering from his mistake-filled last outing and the Bulldogs shutting down the run. As of Tuesday, Sumrall hasn't named his starting quarterback, but I think the hotter hand -- Tramell Jones -- gives OC Buster Faulkner and the Gators the better shot here. ... Georgia 30, Florida 14. No. 6 Utah (-6.5) at Cincinnati Hummer ( Cincinnati +6.5) : On the right week, Cincinnati is capable of beating anyone in the Big 12. We just saw that against Texas Tech. But can the Bearcats do it two weeks in a row? It'll come down to the defense. That unit stepped up against the Red Raiders, holding them to 24 points. Can a unit that ranks 109th nationally in yards allowed per play do that twice in a row? I'm skeptical, especially given how good the Utes are up front. The good news for Cincinnati is its offensive line can match up with anyone. These two offensive fronts lean on each other, and the Utes pull away late. … Utah 24, Cincinnati 20. Crawford (Utah -6.5) : Could the Bearcats put it together in consecutive weeks against top-10 conference opponents? I'll lean no, but it'll be competitive. I was impressed with the Utes' performance last week against Houston, coming back from 10 points down to thwart the Cougars' road upset bid. Utah is now my projected favorite in the conference, and a win this weekend sets up fireworks against BYU on Nov. 7. Just don't get caught looking ahead in this trap spot. ... Utah 34, Cincinnati 24. It's among the most super of superpowers. It's one of those programs with no excuses. It gets just about any player it wants, its realistic expectations are national title or bust, and it's one of the few programs that can lose its starting quarterback and still reasonably be considered the No. 1 team in the country. But now it has to go at least the next several weeks without star quarterback Julian Sayin, who injured his shoulder in the win over Indiana a few weeks ago. There's a quarterback battle to see who steps into the role as the team travels to Los Angeles to face a desperate USC team in a whole lot of trouble. The Trojans are 6-2, but they just got stuffed by Wisconsin in a punishing 24-7 loss, and with a brutal schedule to close, the Lincoln Riley hot seat is flaming. On the plus side, win, and the team is still deep in the College Football Playoff hunt. Ohio State vs USC: Quick Hits It doesn't get any easier for USC with a trip to Indiana next after a week off, and then Maryland, and it all closes at UCLA. Ohio State finishes with three of its last four games in Columbus, hosting Oregon next week. The road game is at Nebraska. This is the first time these two have met since a 24-7 Ohio State win in the 2017 Cotton Bowl. USC has won seven or the last eight in the series goning back to the 1974 Rose Bowl. It has a wonderful 6-2 record, quarterback Jayden Maiava is terrific, and there's still pop and explosion to worry about, but there are flaws. It beat Washington and Penn State, but lost at home to a struggling Oregon, and couldn't get anything going against the Badgers. Ohio State isn't the Ohio State of previous seasons, but it's still good enough to beat anyone else this year. To win, the Buckeyes have to screw up, but USC doesn't take the ball away with just six turnovers forced on the season, and there's little running game to worry about. USC ran well on Rutgers and Louisiana, and that's about it. Slow down the midrange USC passing game, slow down USC. Why USC Will Win If Ohio State didn't exactly go turn-it-loose full-throttle with Julian Sayin under center, what will it do with Luke Fahey and/or Tavien St. Clair? Both are talented prospects, and no matter who is under center, there's still Jeremiah Smith and a loaded receiving corps to throw to, but this is where the offense has to rely on the running game, and it might not be able to do it. The Buckeyes are averaging a pedestrian four yards per carry, and were stuffed by Indiana two weeks ago, gaining just 37 yards. Fahey missed both of his throws against Indiana, and St. Clair has only seen the lightest of mop-up work so far. Ohio State vs USC Prediction, Betting Lines Which team has another gear? Can USC's run defense ball out, and can Jayden Maiava play like the best quarterback on the field? Or will the Ohio State defense step up and keep the big pass plays to a minimum? Yes, Indiana came within a few inches from beating Ohio State, but Josh Hoover only hit 50% of his passes, and only Arch Manning has been able to complete more than 56% against the Buckeyes. Maiava will have a nice day, but the Trojans will stall a bit too often. It won't be pretty, but the Buckeyes will take advantage of a few good field position chances to survive and advance in a relatively low-scoring game. After a bye week, the Buckeyes will now be facing off against the USC Trojans, giving this team another test to overcome. Ohio State remains one of the better teams in the country, but the Trojans will be a challenge. This will be the first game between the two historic programs in Big Ten play, giving each another reason to want to win. The two programs have met multiple times over the years, and it's always been a fun matchup. The Buckeyes did lose starting quarterback Julian Sayin, likely for the season, but this team still has a lot of talent on the roster. Ohio State believes that it can still win a title this season, and the Trojans are just the next team in its way. As the team gets ready for the Trojans, they will be entering the game with a record of 6-1, going 4-0 in Big Ten play. USC comes in with a record of 6-2, going 3-2 in their conference games so far. The Trojans are coming off a bad loss to the Wisconsin Badgers last weekend, giving this team all the desperation they need. The Buckeyes will need to stay focused in this game, looking at this trip as purely business. Entering the game, the Buckeyes are still favored to take down the Trojans, even with the injury to Sayin. According to the ESPN matchup predictor , Ohio State has an 82.8 percent chance of defeating USC on the road this week. For the Buckeyes, making sure to keep the basics the same in this game will be a key. Even without Sayin, the offense should still run through star wide receiver Jeremiah Smith, giving the team a boost. Ohio State may rely even more heavily on Smith to help whoever is under center for this Buckeyes team, giving them a reliable target. Smith is on pace for a truly special season, and the loss of Sayin shouldn't change that fact. The Buckeyes defense will also be tasked with slowing down USC quarterback Jayden Maiava, who has thrown for 2,302 yards with 19 touchdowns and five interceptions. The Trojans rely on their offense to set the tone for the team, and the defense has been a little shaky this season. Kickoff between the two sides is scheduled for 4:30 p.m. PT/7:30 p.m. ET from the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum.

away.blurb: News Sports Business Opinion Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL DB Jay Timmons among Ohio State starters questionable for USC game Brianna Mac Kay Columbus Dispatch Oct. 28, 2026, 8:56 p.m. ET Along with quarterback Julian Sayin and running back Ja'Kobi Jackson , Ohio State football could be without two more starters for the USC game on Oct. 31. Ohio State nickel back Jay Timmons and wide receiver Brandon Inniss are listed as questionable on the Buckeyes ' initial availability report, released by the Big Ten three days before the game. Sayin and Jackson are the only starters among seven Buckeyes already ruled out. Freshman wide receiver Brock Boyd is also listed as questionable. Sayin and Jackson were expected to be out for the USC game, as Sayin is out "indefinitely" with an undisclosed injury he suffered in the fourth quarter of the Indiana game and Jackson underwent foot surgery, according to a report from ESPN on Oct. 21. Timmons made his first appearance in two games against Indiana on Oct. 17 , recording seven tackles, two pass breakups and a forced fumble. But Timmons was pulled from the lineup once again and missed Ohio State's final defensive drives due to an apparent injury. "He plans on traveling," Ohio State coach Ryan Day said Oct. 28. "We'll kind of see how the next couple of days go." After Inniss had missed the Maryland matchup on Oct. 10 with an undisclosed injury, he played the full game against Indiana , logging one catch for 6 yards. The senior is tied for third for the Buckeyes with 11 receptions this season for 158 yards and one touchdown. Ohio State offensive lineman Austin Siereveld was notably left off the availability report after missing the previous two games due to illness. Day stated that Siereveld has returned to full practice this week, and he expects the senior to be an option, though is uncertain he'll be able to play the full game. away.headline: Where Ohio State football’s offensive line health stands going into USC game
away.blurb: However, Daniels was injured late in a Sept. 12 loss at Texas. He did not return until an Oct. 17 win at Indiana. COLUMBUS, Ohio — Ohio State football fielded a variety of offensive line combinations through the first half of its regular season, with injuries forcing movement up front. Coming off a bye week and heading into Saturday’s game at USC, coach Ryan Day expects the unit to be as healthy as it has been this season. “We should have a full week of practice and a full arsenal of guys up front, so that is a huge deal going into this game,” Day said during a radio hit Monday on 97.1 The Fan. “We know that the offensive line, we’re going to lean on them more to be the guys who lead this team — along with our seniors, along with Jeremiah (Smith), running backs that are running real hard. But it all starts up front.” The Buckeyes opened the season with Ian Moore, Luke Montgomery, Carson Hinzman, Austin Siereveld and Phillip Daniels starting from left to right. During his absence, Ohio State originally moved Siereveld to right tackle and started Gabe VanSickle at right guard. That changed Oct. 10, when an illness sidelined Siereveld hours before a matchup with Maryland. VanSickle moved to right tackle and Jake Cook started at right guard as a result. The Buckeyes moved VanSickle back to right guard when Daniels returned to play right tackle the following week. The starting combination with a full roster remains unclear, though Day said Siereveld would start at tackle if healthy when asked ahead of the Indiana game. Health up front is always paramount, but that is especially true for a team making a change at quarterback. Julian Sayin was injured late in the win at Indiana, and the Buckeyes are preparing for him to miss the remainder of the season. As a result, freshman Luke Fahey or sophomore Tavien St. Clair will start Saturday at USC. “These guys have played a lot of football before,” Day said of the offensive line. “We’re in that huddle and you’ve got a young quarterback right there — I mean, they’re going to be looking to him, but he’s going to be looking at them. I’ve got to give them credit already. They’re already building up the confidence of our young quarterbacks.” ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. away.headline: Ryan Day declines to name Ohio State football's starting quarterback for USC
away.blurb: Fahey replaced Sayin in the fourth quarter of the Buckeyes’ win at Indiana on Oct. 17 after he left with an injury . When Sayin was sacked by defensive lineman Mario Landino, the collision appeared to injure his right throwing arm, and he was later in a cast. He remains out indefinitely. Ohio State coach Ryan Day declined to name a starting quarterback following practice on Oct. 28. Day said freshman Luke Fahey and sophomore Tavien St. Clair have both practiced well as the Buckeyes prepare for this week’s game at USC without Julian Sayin behind center. “Both will be ready to play,” Day said. “Guys on the team have confidence that if both were put in the game, that they can do their job.” Day did little to tip his hand publicly about the pecking order at the position and sidestepped a question about whether he knew who would start against the Trojans . “Things have progressed this week similar to the way they have in the past,” Day said. “I’ll just leave it at that, keep preparing and play the game on Saturday.” Fahey has been seen as most likely to assume the starting role after he emerged as the No. 2 quarterback during preseason practices, surpassing St. Clair, who had arrived at Ohio State a year earlier as a decorated five-star prospect from Bellefontaine. But the Buckeyes began a midseason competition while they were idle last week, giving both Fahey and St. Clair first-team reps in practice. Nether has seen significant snaps for the Buckeyes. Fahey has completed nine of 13 passes for 203 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions in four games. St. Clair has completed five of nine passes for 52 yards and one touchdown with one interception in three games since last season. Joey Kaufman covers Ohio State football for The Columbus Dispatch. home.headline: DB Jay Timmons among Ohio State starters questionable for USC game
home.blurb: News Sports Business Opinion Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL DB Jay Timmons among Ohio State starters questionable for USC game Brianna Mac Kay Columbus Dispatch Oct. 28, 2026, 8:56 p.m. ET Along with quarterback Julian Sayin and running back Ja'Kobi Jackson , Ohio State football could be without two more starters for the USC game on Oct. 31. Ohio State nickel back Jay Timmons and wide receiver Brandon Inniss are listed as questionable on the Buckeyes ' initial availability report, released by the Big Ten three days before the game. Sayin and Jackson are the only starters among seven Buckeyes already ruled out. Freshman wide receiver Brock Boyd is also listed as questionable. Sayin and Jackson were expected to be out for the USC game, as Sayin is out "indefinitely" with an undisclosed injury he suffered in the fourth quarter of the Indiana game and Jackson underwent foot surgery, according to a report from ESPN on Oct. 21. Timmons made his first appearance in two games against Indiana on Oct. 17 , recording seven tackles, two pass breakups and a forced fumble. But Timmons was pulled from the lineup once again and missed Ohio State's final defensive drives due to an apparent injury. "He plans on traveling," Ohio State coach Ryan Day said Oct. 28. "We'll kind of see how the next couple of days go." After Inniss had missed the Maryland matchup on Oct. 10 with an undisclosed injury, he played the full game against Indiana , logging one catch for 6 yards. The senior is tied for third for the Buckeyes with 11 receptions this season for 158 yards and one touchdown. Ohio State offensive lineman Austin Siereveld was notably left off the availability report after missing the previous two games due to illness. Day stated that Siereveld has returned to full practice this week, and he expects the senior to be an option, though is uncertain he'll be able to play the full game. home.headline: Where Ohio State football’s offensive line health stands going into USC game
home.blurb: However, Daniels was injured late in a Sept. 12 loss at Texas. He did not return until an Oct. 17 win at Indiana. COLUMBUS, Ohio — Ohio State football fielded a variety of offensive line combinations through the first half of its regular season, with injuries forcing movement up front. Coming off a bye week and heading into Saturday’s game at USC, coach Ryan Day expects the unit to be as healthy as it has been this season. “We should have a full week of practice and a full arsenal of guys up front, so that is a huge deal going into this game,” Day said during a radio hit Monday on 97.1 The Fan. “We know that the offensive line, we’re going to lean on them more to be the guys who lead this team — along with our seniors, along with Jeremiah (Smith), running backs that are running real hard. But it all starts up front.” The Buckeyes opened the season with Ian Moore, Luke Montgomery, Carson Hinzman, Austin Siereveld and Phillip Daniels starting from left to right. During his absence, Ohio State originally moved Siereveld to right tackle and started Gabe VanSickle at right guard. That changed Oct. 10, when an illness sidelined Siereveld hours before a matchup with Maryland. VanSickle moved to right tackle and Jake Cook started at right guard as a result. The Buckeyes moved VanSickle back to right guard when Daniels returned to play right tackle the following week. The starting combination with a full roster remains unclear, though Day said Siereveld would start at tackle if healthy when asked ahead of the Indiana game. Health up front is always paramount, but that is especially true for a team making a change at quarterback. Julian Sayin was injured late in the win at Indiana, and the Buckeyes are preparing for him to miss the remainder of the season. As a result, freshman Luke Fahey or sophomore Tavien St. Clair will start Saturday at USC. “These guys have played a lot of football before,” Day said of the offensive line. “We’re in that huddle and you’ve got a young quarterback right there — I mean, they’re going to be looking to him, but he’s going to be looking at them. I’ve got to give them credit already. They’re already building up the confidence of our young quarterbacks.” ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. Pete Fiutak Thu, October 29, 2026 at 2:02 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Here's the punchline – both Baylor and UCF are 4-3 overall and 2-2 in Big 12 play. On one side, Baylor lost on the road to Kansas in a 25-24 fight, and that was it. Head coach Dave Aranda was fired, defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman is the interim head man, and the team needs this win with a tough November coming up. However, win in Orlando, beat Iowa State at home, and boom – the Bears are bowl-eligible. UCF lost on the road to Houston and Oklahoma State, and then it changed the national landscape – and got Scott Frost his first huge win in his second round with the Knights – with a 39-31 victory over BYU. With a very favorable finishing kick, UCF has to keep the momentum going. Baylor vs UCF: Quick Hits Baylor has the home date against Iowa State next, and then there's a problem – at BYU, Texas Tech, at Houston. UCF goes to Kansas after this, and then plays Arizona State, Iowa State, and goes to Colorado. None of those four are likely to go to a bowl game. It's the fourth meeting between the two. Baylor won 30-3 last year and won 36-35 in 2023, but UCF won a wild 52-42 Fiesta Bowl to end the 2013 season. How To Watch Baylor vs UCF Date: Friday, October 30, 2026 Game Time: 7:30 PM ET TV: ESPN Location: Acrisure Bounce House, Orlando, FL – Week 9 Schedule, Game Previews – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predicting the First CFP Top 25 – CFN Week 9 Expert Picks Why Baylor Will Win The defense is taking the ball away in bunches. The run defense has been fantastic – Kansas ripped it up last week, but that was an anomaly – but the takeaways have been the biggest help, with 13 overall and at least two in four games. UCF doesn't have to get the running game going to win, but it's a huge help going 4-1 when running for more than 100 yards. Baylor has held four teams to under 100, but … Why UCF Will Win UCF isn't having a problem with turnovers. It has only given it up seven times, didn't turn it over against BYU, and it's +5 overall in turnover margin. So really, how did UCF beat BYU? The running game was effective enough – even if it wasn't dominant – and the passing game was fearless, and that's how the Knights have to play. They don't have to bomb away, but they should take the midrange plays against a Baylor pass defense that can get to the quarterback but is susceptible to quick hits. Baylor vs UCF Prediction, Betting Lines UCF needs to capitalize on the momentum, and it will. The Knights are 4-0 in the Bounce House, and 0-3 away from it. Baylor hung 55 at Arizona State and suffered two one-point losses away from Waco, but now it has to deal with the coaching drama and all the changes. The team will play hard and well for Klanderman, but the UCF offense will be just a bit more effective. Baylor (4-3, 2-2 Big 12); UCF (4-3, 2-2). Last meeting: Baylor beat UCF 30-3 on Nov. 1, 2025, in Waco What's at stake? This is an important opportunity for Baylor to get its season back on track. The Bears have dropped consecutive games against TCU and Kansas and now enter a new chapter under interim head coach Joe Klanderman following Dave Aranda's dismissal . At 4-3, Baylor cannot afford to let another conference game slip away if it hopes to remain competitive in the Big 12 standings. A road win would also give Klanderman a strong start to his tenure. UCF enters the matchup with momentum after defeating No. 2 BYU 39-31 in double overtime. The Knights have shown they can compete with the conference's top teams, making Friday's matchup an important test for Baylor's defense. When Baylor has the ball Baylor's passing attack will be one of its biggest advantages in this matchup. The Bears average 278.9 passing yards per game, and UCF surrenders 239.7 passing yards per game. Quarterback DJ Lagway will need to take advantage of that matchup and find opportunities downfield. Wide receiver Gavin Freeman has been one of Baylor's most consistent weapons, recording 58 receptions for 678 yards through seven games. His ability to create plays and stretch the field could be important against a UCF defense that has struggled more against the pass than the run. However, Baylor will need to establish a more consistent rushing attack. Dawson Pendergrass leads the Bears with 331 rushing yards, but the offense has averaged just 146.1 rushing yards per game. Finding balance between the run and pass will be important in keeping UCF's defense from focusing entirely on Lagway. When UCF has the ball The Knights rely on a balanced offensive attack led by quarterback Keyone Jenkins and running back Duke Watson. Jenkins has thrown for 1,099 yards and 11 touchdowns while Watson leads the team with 577 rushing yards and three touchdowns. Baylor's defensive front will need to pressure Jenkins and limit Watson's ability to establish the run. The Bears rank third nationally in sacks, giving them an opportunity to disrupt UCF's offensive rhythm. If Baylor can force third-and-long situations and create turnovers, it could make things difficult for a UCF offense that is coming off an emotional double-overtime victory. Baylor enters this matchup with plenty to prove after consecutive losses and a coaching change. While UCF has momentum following its win over BYU, the Bears have the defensive talent to make this a difficult matchup for the Knights. I expect Baylor to lean on its defense and take advantage of its passing game, with Freeman playing an important role. The Bears will need to clean up their mistakes and avoid giving UCF extra opportunities, but the Bears will find a way to get their first win under Klanderman. Score: Baylor 27, UCF 24. UCF enters the game riding high after stunning No. 2 BYU 39-31 in double overtime for the Knights' biggest win since joining the Big 12. Meanwhile, Baylor is beginning a new era after firing head coach Dave Aranda following Saturday's 25-24 loss to Kansas, with defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman taking over as interim head coach. Despite taking very different paths to get here, Baylor and UCF enter Friday night's game with identical 4-3 overall records and 2-2 marks in Big 12 play. For UCF, the question is whether Scott Frost's team can build off its breakthrough win or suffer a letdown. For Baylor, it's about what kind of response the Bears will have in their first game without Aranda. Here is everything you need to know about Baylor vs. UCF in Week 9, including our prediction and pick for Friday night's Big 12 matchup. Baylor vs. UCF Odds Spread: UCF -1.5 Over/Under: 48.5 Moneyline: UCF -120/Baylor +100 Odds as of Tuesday afternoon. Odds are subject to change. The Biggest Question: How do the emotions play a factor? The emotions on both sides of this game are tremendous. UCF is coming off of one of the biggest wins in program history over No. 2 BYU in double overtime at home. Now, they have to put that in the rearview mirror and take on Baylor. What' done is done. Have the Knights spent the last week in celebration mode? And then, on the other side, head coach Dave Aranda was fired on Sunday by Baylor. How does the team respond? How does defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman do in the interim role? There are so many unknowns going into this game, beyond the X's and O's, that ultimately will determine the outcome. Baylor vs. UCF Prediction and Pick Prediction: UCF 23, Baylor 20 It's a short week for both teams, but the good news for UCF is that they're playing their second-straight home game after a bye week. They haven't had to leave the friendly confines of Central Florida in nearly a month. Meantime, Baylor is getting set for its 3rd road game in its last four match ups, and their first without Aranda. In games like this, I try to find a nugget to sway me one way or the other, and here's what I've found: Baylor leads the Big 12 with 27 sacks in seven games. But one of the many things that UCF has done well with Keyone Jenkins is move the pocket, get rid of the ball quickly and avoid pressure in the backfield. BYU only had one sack last week against UCF, and the Knights have only allowed 10 in seven games, good for fourth fewest in the Big 12 Conference. Negating the pass rush by Baylor opens up a lot of opportunities for the UCF offense, and I believe that will be a game-changer on Friday night. Baylor has proven it can play with, and beat, some of the lesser Big 12 teams like Colorado and Arizona State. But even against just slightly better competition, TCU and Kansas, they came up short. UCF is one of the more underrated teams in the country, which I've been telling you since August. And despite their injuries, they're playing solid, team football, and that culminated with a with vs. BYU. But it was not a fluke. They led Houston in the second half on the road. They were beating Oklahoma State in Stillwater early in the game. This team can play with the best. Now, they get a chance to play one of the worst? I'll not overcomplicate this and take UCF to win and cover. Baylor's run defense ranks 4th in the Big 12, but they've already played the three worst running teams in the conference in Colorado, Arizona State and TCU. Now, they get Duke Watson, Jenkins and the rest of the run game going on Friday night to seal a win. UCF wins. UCF covers. Mandatory Credit: Raymond Carlin III-Imagn Images College Football Week 9 Friday night college football previews. Baylor vs. UCF Three games are on the college football card for Friday night, headlined by Baylor vs. UCF. Both teams are in very difficult spots here, as the Knights just upset BYU at home in overtime last week and the Bears fired head coach Dave Aranda after losing at home to Kansas. On a night with the MAC, American, and Big 12, we have Kent State as a rare home favorite, a mediocre Tulane team laying double digits, and then the coin flip in Orlando. Despite the tricky circumstances with Baylor and UCF, that’s the game of the night and the game that deserves the most attention. Odds from Circa Sports as of October 28, 1:20 p.m. PT ; check out our Circa Betting Splits and DraftKings Betting Splits . See all of our Week 9 College Football Picks and Predictions . Baylor at UCF (-1, 48) Prediction Friday, 7:30 p.m. ET (ESPN) Baylor invades the Bounce House this week and we’ll see if interim head coach Joe Klanderman can put some more pep in the steps of the Bears. It felt like Aranda was simply holding on for dear life with this gig for a while and it finally came to a head this past week with a blocked field goal that led to a loss against the Jayhawks. I watched Klanderman’s media availability this week and he comes across as a very honest, very poignant guy who isn’t going to BS this team about what’s going on. I appreciate that. In this day and age, I think the players do as well. Klanderman will continue to call the defense, while longtime up-and-comer Jake Spavital has creative freedom on offense. The 41-year-old Spavital was Texas A&M’s OC by the age of 30 and even was Texas State’s head coach for four rough seasons. But he’s always been pretty highly-regarded in the coaching world and now he has free reign of the offense. By no means has the offense been good, but Aranda was kind of a passive guy and there wasn’t a lot of explosiveness or aggressiveness to Baylor’s offensive profile. With a lot of money invested in DJ Lagway, let’s see if Spavital can unlock something. Lagway has only completed 52.1% of his passes and only has 26 carries for 19 yards, so it’s been a struggle to get him free. Leading rusher Dawson Pendergrass only has 3.5 yards per carry. The Baylor offensive line needs to be better, but we should see an improvement in effort and focus for this week. UCF head coach Scott Frost brought in Keyone Jenkins as an insurance policy behind expected starter Alonza Barrett III from James Madison. Instead, it has been Jenkins, the FIU transfer, who has carried this team in Barrett’s absence. He sports an 11/3 TD/INT ratio and a completion rate butting up against 70%, while transfer RB Duke Watson has rushed for 6.8 yards per carry. While Baylor’s defensive numbers stand up a lot better, as the Bears are 17th in the nation in yards per play allowed, it should be noted that Jeff Sagarin has a strength of schedule gap of 30 spots between the two teams, as UCF has already played three top-30 teams per Sagarin and Baylor has not played any. The Knights rank 27th in SOS and the Bears are 57th, with a big difference in Big 12 opponents. UCF has played TCU, Houston, Oklahoma State, and BYU. Baylor has played Colorado, Arizona State, TCU, and Kansas. Of that group, Arizona State is the only one with a winning record and the only one without a losing conference record. It’s a tough spot for UCF coming off of the BYU win, but they aren’t traveling, they don’t have the internal tumult, and Jenkins has definitively outplayed Lagway this season and even done so against better competition. Other Friday Games Tulane (-10, 47) at Charlotte: This is a hefty number for Tulane, a team that ranks 99th with -.51 net points per drive per Brian Fremeau of BCFToys. Of course, Charlotte is 134th out of 138 teams, so we’re talking about one of the worst programs in the nation. The Green Wave have not gotten good QB play out of either Kadin Semonza or Trace Johnson, with 18 total sacks and a 5/5 TD/INT ratio. Even though the Green Wave have a great running game and maybe that will be enough, winning by margin requires taking care of the football and avoiding negative plays. Charlotte has poor run defense numbers, but it should be noted that they’ve allowed 4.55 YPC to FBS opponents and allowed 5.36 YPC in the loss to The Citadel. Kent State (-10, 46.5) at Sacramento State: Historical outliers are scary and Kent State being favored like this on the road hasn’t happened since 2022. That could be part of the reason why we’ve seen money come in on the Hornets and against the Golden Flashes. It’s also just ludicrous to think about Kent State facing these kinds of expectations, but Sac State might be the worst FBS team we’ve ever seen. If Kent wins and covers, that might solidify it, but that’s an enormous ask and the market seems to think it’s too big of one. away.headline: 5 Questionable Decisions That Defined Dave Aranda's Baylor Tenure
away.blurb: 5 Questionable Decisions That Defined Dave Aranda's Baylor Tenure Skip to main content SI.COM Here are five of the most questionable decisions of Aranda's Baylor tenure. Aranda had reason to overhaul Baylor's defensive staff following the 2022 season, but his choice of replacement proved questionable. Continuing to direct the defense while overseeing the entire program raised questions about whether Aranda had taken on too much. Although his defensive expertise was never in doubt, the arrangement potentially limited the attention he could devote to recruiting, roster construction and other head coaching duties. Dave Aranda's tenure at Baylor peaked in 2021, when the Bears won a program-record 12 games, captured the Big 12 championship and claimed a Sugar Bowl victory. Nearly five years later, he was fired following Saturday's 25-24 loss at Kansas, finishing his six-plus seasons in Waco with a 40-40 record. Baylor's decline can't be traced to a single mistake, but several of Aranda's decisions played a role in the program's inability to sustain its success. Some made sense at the time but ultimately backfired, while others were mistakes he later acknowledged. 1. Rebilas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Aranda's emphasis on player development helped establish the culture behind Baylor's 2021 championship, but that same philosophy arguably kept the Bears from adapting quickly enough to college football's changing roster landscape. Aranda's emphasis on player development helped establish the culture behind Baylor's 2021 championship, but that same philosophy arguably kept the Bears from adapting quickly enough to college football's changing roster landscape. Baylor added only 10 scholarship transfers during Aranda's first three seasons before bringing in 12 during the 2023 cycle. While other programs increasingly used the portal to address immediate needs, the Bears remained more reliant on developing players already on their roster. Aranda later acknowledged struggling with bringing in transfers when doing so could mean passing over players he had recruited and developed. That reluctance became particularly costly following the 2021 season, when Baylor lost several important contributors, including Jalen Pitre, JT Woods, Terrel Bernard and Abram Smith. Replacing that experience and production was never going to be easy, but the transfer portal offered opportunities to address weaknesses before they became bigger problems. Instead, Baylor struggled to maintain the depth and physicality that had helped it win the conference championship. home.blurb: ESPN's Pete Thamel reported Tuesday that UCF starting quarterback Alonza Barnett III will not start Saturday, still recovering from the hamstring injury he suffered Sept. 12 at Pittsburgh. He was officially listed as questionable on the Big 12's first availability reported released Wednesday. "I think he's making really good progress," Frost said. "He looks good. He's doing a lot of things. I want to make sure he's ready to go if we put him out there. That position, you might not have to run for 10 plays, and then you've got to run away from some really big guys trying to get you." UCF has already ruled out running back Taevion Swint , wide receiver Caleb Rollerson, linebacker Lewis Carter and offensive linemen Owen Spell and Tyler Gibson. Slot receiver Duane Thomas Jr., who has missed each of the first six games, is questionable along with center Jacob Maiava. BYU is the highest-ranked opponent to ever play at UCF's on-campus stadium. UCF's starting quarterback Alonza Barnett III is not expected to start due to a hamstring injury. BYU will be without reigning Big 12 Offensive Player of the Year, running back LJ Martin. ORLANDO — After a week of rest, UCF's football team prepares for its biggest test in 2026. Fresh off their bye week, the Knights (3-3, 1-2) host BYU (6-0, 3-0), ranked No. 2 in The Associated Press' Top 25 and No. 3 in the US LBM Coaches Poll , at 3:30 p.m. Saturday, Oct. 24 . The Cougars, who snapped Notre Dame's 16-game winning streak last weekend in a 28-24 thriller, are the highest-ranked opponent to visit the Acrisure Bounce House . "The motivation and drive is that we're right there ," UCF offensive tackle Preston Cushman said. "We're going in and we're going against top-25 teams, and we're rolling them up for the first three quarters. And then it just goes downhill after that. … We're going to play the No. 2 team in the nation this week, another Big 12 opponent, so we're excited for the opportunity. We're right there on so many levels (to) just playing a complete game like we talk about all the time." The Knights have a 6-6 home record against nationally ranked opponents since opening their on-campus stadium in 2007, but an 0-3 mark against consensus top-10 teams. Scott Frost oversaw two of those victories in back-to-back weeks near the conclusion of the 2017 campaign — against longtime American Conference rivals South Florida and Memphis. "It's homecoming. It's the Big 12. Everybody's pretty close," Frost said. "I think BYU's the best of the bunch. There are some arguments to be made for other teams, too, but I think they've done a really good job. They're big and long and physical. They've got a really good quarterback. There are no holes. There are solid players everywhere, and they know what they're doing; they're well-coached. home.headline: UCF's Scott Frost Shares Injury Updates Ahead of Space Game
home.blurb: Coach Scott Frost said running back Taevion Swint will be back quickly, and linebacker Lewis Carter could be a game-time decision this week . He added that if the senior isn't available against the Baylor Bears, he'll likely be a game-time decision next Saturday against the Kansas Jayhawks . Carter has missed every conference game this season. He went into the medical tent for a knee injury at the end of Week 3's win over the Georgia State Panthers and was ruled out early for the next game. UCF's Scott Frost Shares Injury Updates Ahead of Space Game UCFRoundtable 372 Members • 1,444 Posts UCFRoundtable UCFRoundtable Related stories (Mike Watters/Imagn Images) (Mike Watters/Imagn Images) UCF's Scott Frost Shares Injury Updates Ahead of Space Game Demetrius Montero Partner Oct 27, 2026 9:00 PM Published Oct 27, 2026 9:00 PM Updated Oct 28, 2026 2:36 PM Fresh off an historic upset, the Knights could regain dynamic playmaker Taevion Swint and defensive leader Lewis Carter just in time for Friday’s high-stakes mission against Baylor. More Videos The UCF Knights made program history in upsetting the then-No. 2 BYU Cougars , and a few key players are on the cusp of returning for Friday's Space Game. Swint's injury occurred in practice, and Frost said he started limping after a "nothing play." The redshirt freshman missed his first game of the season , leaving room for Landen Chambers to step up in his absence. UCF has relied on the speedster to make plays in the run game and on special teams. Swint's rushed for 162 yards and two touchdowns on 32 carries, and returned seven kickoffs for 209 yards. He scored his first touchdown in the season opener against the Bethune-Cookman Wildcats, and the second in the Big 12 home opener against the TCU Horned Frogs . The Knights have missed their defensive quarterback, especially in highly contested losses against the then-No. 20 Houston Cougars and then-No. 18 Oklahoma State Cowboys . The senior had a career season last year after transferring from Oklahoma . Carter led the team with 92 tackles and set career highs in tackles for loss, sacks, and fumbles. He became a star at UCF. While at Oklahoma, he was a reserve linebacker and special teams player. Wisconsin transfer Tackett Curtis, the team's leading tackler, has stepped up in Carter's absence. Curtis has 42 tackles (18 solo, 24 assisted), one sack, one fumble recovery, one pass deflection and two interceptions. The Knights are getting healthy at the right time. They aim to build on an upset win and collect two more wins to break a two-year bowl drought. Friday's game against Baylor is one of the more interesting weekday matchups . The program fired coach David Aranda, and Joe Klanderman is the interim coach. UCF's eight-game Space Game winning streak ended in heartbreaking fashion as Houston caught the game-winning interception against former Knights quarterback Davi Belfort. UCF Injury Report Raises Concerns Ahead of Top-10 Showdown With BYU
home.blurb: The Knights listed 10 players, including starting quarterback Alonza Barnett III and freshman running back Taevion Swing (162 yards), as questionable or worse on Thursday. Another six players – 4 defense, 1 offense, 1 special teams – are probable for the week's top-10 home test vs. No. 2 BYU, which is hot off its nationally-regarded win over then-No. 2 Notre Dame in Provo. It'll be up to Jenkins, who left the game for UCF in the third quarter of the Houston loss , to test BYU through the air on Saturday with Barnett unavailable, and it'll come as the senior backup grows comfortable as his team's signal caller. The Scott Frost staff displays trust in Jenkins, but the payout hasn't come in the win column following two Big 12 losses at Oklahoma State and Houston; Both losses saw Jenkins combine for 518 passing yards, 5 touchdowns and two interceptions on 53 attempts. To stay within such a low spread, UCF needs a big day out of Jenkins and the offense to keep pace with a BYU squad intent on keeping its perfect 3-0 Big 12 record intact. It's hard to bet against the Cougars, but this home return for UCF after a week off certainly factors into the math as Frost and company look for a big one this weekend when the league's frontrunners come to town.
